google_accesscontextmanager_access_level: `google_accesscontextmanager_access_level` defines a condition (device state, IP range, geography) that must hold for a request to be granted access under VPC Service Controls' own Access Context Manager.
google_accesscontextmanager_access_polic: `google_accesscontextmanager_access_policy` is the top-level container for Access Context Manager, holding every access level and service perimeter defined for an organization.
google_accesscontextmanager_authorized_o: `google_accesscontextmanager_authorized_orgs_desc` defines a set of trusted external organization(s) whose own identities are exempted from certain VPC Service Controls restrictions.
google_accesscontextmanager_gcp_user_acc: `google_accesscontextmanager_gcp_user_access_binding` restricts which Access Context Manager access level(s) a specific group of Google Workspace users must satisfy to reach Google Cloud resources.
google_accesscontextmanager_service_peri: `google_accesscontextmanager_service_perimeter` defines a boundary around a set of Google Cloud project(s) and service(s), blocking data exfiltration to and from resources outside the perimeter -- the core VPC Service Controls enforcement resource.
google_aiplatform_agent: `google_aiplatform_agent` registers a deployable AI agent within Vertex AI's Agent Builder surface (now documented under the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform), the unit an Agent Engine deployment or the Agent Studio low-code builder operates on.
google_aiplatform_aiplatform_online_eval: `google_aiplatform_aiplatform_online_evaluator` configures the Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service to continuously score a live, running application's own conversation sessions against a set of evaluation metrics, rather than a one-off offline evaluation run.
google_aiplatform_artifact: `google_aiplatform_artifact` records a single, versioned piece of data (a dataset snapshot, a model file, a metric report) produced or consumed by a Vertex AI ML Metadata pipeline, so lineage between pipeline steps can be traced.
google_aiplatform_batch_prediction_job: `google_aiplatform_batch_prediction_job` runs a model against a large, offline batch of input data in one pass and writes the predictions to Cloud Storage or BigQuery, rather than serving them from a live online endpoint.
google_aiplatform_cached_content: `google_aiplatform_cached_content` stores a large, reusable prompt payload (e.g. a lengthy document or video) on the server side so repeated Gemini API calls referencing it avoid re-uploading and re-processing the same content, lowering latency and cost.
google_aiplatform_context: `google_aiplatform_context` groups related Vertex AI ML Metadata artifacts and executions together under one logical unit, e.g. all the artifacts produced across a single experiment run or pipeline execution.
google_aiplatform_custom_job: `google_aiplatform_custom_job` runs caller-supplied training code (a container image or a Python package) on managed Vertex AI compute, for training scenarios a built-in AutoML or pre-built algorithm doesn't cover.
google_aiplatform_data_labeling_job: `google_aiplatform_data_labeling_job` sends a dataset out to human labelers (Google's own workforce or a caller-specified one) to annotate, producing the labeled training data a supervised model is trained on.
google_aiplatform_dataset: `google_aiplatform_dataset` represents a managed collection of training data (image, tabular, text, or video) that Vertex AI's own AutoML and custom training jobs can reference directly.
google_aiplatform_dataset_version: `google_aiplatform_dataset_version` is a specific, immutable snapshot of a Vertex AI dataset's own contents at a point in time, letting a training job pin to exactly the data it was trained on even as the dataset itself keeps changing.
google_aiplatform_deployment_resource_po: `google_aiplatform_deployment_resource_pool` is a shared pool of compute nodes that more than one model deployment can be co-located on, so several models can share the same underlying machines instead of each needing its own dedicated endpoint capacity.
google_aiplatform_endpoint: `google_aiplatform_endpoint` is the deployed, servable HTTP target a Vertex AI model is attached to for online prediction, handling request routing and traffic splitting across one or more deployed model versions.
google_aiplatform_entity_type: `google_aiplatform_entity_type` defines a category of entity (e.g. `user` or `product`) within a legacy Vertex AI Feature Store, grouping the feature(s) computed for every instance of that entity.
google_aiplatform_evaluation_item: `google_aiplatform_evaluation_item` is a single scored case (one input, its generated output, and its evaluation result) produced as part of a Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service evaluation run.
google_aiplatform_evaluation_metric: `google_aiplatform_evaluation_metric` defines a specific scoring criterion (a built-in metric like coherence or safety, or a caller-defined rubric) the Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service applies when scoring model or agent output.
google_aiplatform_evaluation_run: `google_aiplatform_evaluation_run` is a single execution of the Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service against a dataset or evaluation set, producing scored results per item across the configured metric(s).
google_aiplatform_evaluation_set: `google_aiplatform_evaluation_set` is a reusable, named collection of evaluation input cases (prompts, reference outputs, or both) that a Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service evaluation run is executed against.
google_aiplatform_execution: `google_aiplatform_execution` records a single run of a step (a training job, a data transformation) within Vertex AI's own ML Metadata lineage graph, connecting the artifact(s) it consumed to the artifact(s) it produced.
google_aiplatform_experiment: `google_aiplatform_experiment` groups related Vertex AI training runs together so their own parameters and metrics can be compared side by side, the top-level container Vertex AI Experiments organizes runs under.
google_aiplatform_feature: `google_aiplatform_feature` defines a single named, typed ML feature (e.g. `age` or `click_count`) within a Vertex AI Feature Store's own feature group or legacy entity type.
google_aiplatform_feature_group: `google_aiplatform_feature_group` is a named collection of related feature(s) in Vertex AI's current Feature Store, backed by a BigQuery source table the feature values are read from.
google_aiplatform_feature_online_store: `google_aiplatform_feature_online_store` is the low-latency serving layer in Vertex AI's current Feature Store that feature values are synced into for real-time online lookup during model inference.
google_aiplatform_feature_view: `google_aiplatform_feature_view` defines which feature(s), from which feature group(s), are synced into a specific Vertex AI Feature Online Store for serving.
google_aiplatform_featurestore: `google_aiplatform_featurestore` is the top-level container in Vertex AI's legacy Feature Store, holding the entity type(s) and their own feature definitions used for both training and online serving.
google_aiplatform_hyperparameter_tuning_: `google_aiplatform_hyperparameter_tuning_job` runs many trials of a training job automatically, each with a different combination of hyperparameter values, to find the combination that best optimizes a chosen objective metric.
google_aiplatform_index: `google_aiplatform_index` is a Vertex AI Vector Search index built over a set of embedding vectors, enabling fast approximate nearest-neighbor lookup once deployed to an index endpoint.
google_aiplatform_index_endpoint: `google_aiplatform_index_endpoint` is the deployed, servable target a Vertex AI Vector Search index is attached to, handling nearest-neighbor query traffic against the index's own embeddings.
google_aiplatform_memory: `google_aiplatform_memory` is a single stored memory (a durable fact or preference extracted from past conversations) held in Vertex AI Agent Engine's own Memory Bank, retrievable to personalize a future agent interaction.
google_aiplatform_metadata_schema: `google_aiplatform_metadata_schema` defines the structure (field names and types) that Vertex AI ML Metadata artifacts, executions, or contexts of a given type must conform to.
google_aiplatform_metadata_store: `google_aiplatform_metadata_store` is the top-level container for a region's own Vertex AI ML Metadata -- every artifact, execution, and context tracking lineage across that region's training and pipeline runs lives inside one.
google_aiplatform_model_deployment_monit: `google_aiplatform_model_deployment_monitoring_job` continuously watches a deployed Vertex AI endpoint's own live prediction traffic for training-serving skew and data drift, alerting when incoming data diverges from what the model was trained on.
google_aiplatform_nas_job: `google_aiplatform_nas_job` runs Vertex AI Neural Architecture Search, which automatically searches a defined space of possible model architectures to find one that best optimizes a chosen objective (e.g. accuracy under a latency budget).
google_aiplatform_notebook_execution_job: `google_aiplatform_notebook_execution_job` runs a Vertex AI Workbench notebook's own cells end to end as a scheduled or one-off batch job, without a human attached to an interactive session.
google_aiplatform_notebook_runtime_templ: `google_aiplatform_notebook_runtime_template` defines the reusable compute and networking configuration (machine type, image, network) a Vertex AI Colab Enterprise notebook runtime is created from.
google_aiplatform_online_evaluator: `google_aiplatform_online_evaluator` configures the Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service to continuously score a live, running application's own conversation sessions against a set of evaluation metrics, rather than a one-off offline evaluation run.
google_aiplatform_persistent_resource: `google_aiplatform_persistent_resource` is a long-running, pre-provisioned compute cluster on Vertex AI that multiple training jobs or pipeline runs can reuse, avoiding the provisioning delay of spinning up fresh compute for each one.
google_aiplatform_pipeline_job: `google_aiplatform_pipeline_job` runs a Vertex AI Pipelines (Kubeflow Pipelines-based) workflow -- an ordered graph of ML step(s) such as data prep, training, and evaluation -- as a single orchestrated execution.
google_aiplatform_rag_corpora: `google_aiplatform_rag_corpora` is a RagCorpus in Vertex AI's RAG Engine, a container holding the imported document(s) (RagFiles) a retrieval-augmented generation application retrieves grounding context from.
google_aiplatform_reasoning_engine: `google_aiplatform_reasoning_engine` deploys an agent (built with a framework like LangChain or the Agent Development Kit) onto Vertex AI Agent Engine's own managed runtime, giving it a servable endpoint without the caller having to manage the underlying infrastructure.
google_aiplatform_run: `google_aiplatform_run` records a single execution instance grouped under a Vertex AI Experiment, capturing the parameters and metrics logged for that specific training or evaluation attempt.
google_aiplatform_sandbox_environment: `google_aiplatform_sandbox_environment` is an isolated, managed execution environment Vertex AI Agent Engine's Code Execution capability runs caller- or agent-generated code inside, so it can't affect anything outside its own sandbox.
google_aiplatform_sandbox_environment_te: `google_aiplatform_sandbox_environment_template` defines the reusable configuration (base image, resource limits) a Vertex AI Agent Engine sandbox environment is created from.
google_aiplatform_schedule: `google_aiplatform_schedule` triggers a Vertex AI Pipelines pipeline job to run automatically on a recurring cron-style schedule, instead of only on manual or event-driven invocation.
google_aiplatform_semantic_governance_po: `google_aiplatform_semantic_governance_policy` defines a rule (e.g. a content or data-access restriction) enforced across an organization's own AI agents and applications on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, part of its governance layer for AI usage.
google_aiplatform_session: `google_aiplatform_session` is a single, stateful conversation between a user and an agent deployed on Vertex AI Agent Engine, holding the chronological sequence of message(s) and action(s) exchanged during that interaction.
google_aiplatform_specialist_pool: `google_aiplatform_specialist_pool` defines a named pool of human reviewer(s) (Google-managed or customer-managed) available to a Vertex AI data labeling job for annotating training data.
google_aiplatform_study: `google_aiplatform_study` is the top-level configuration for a Vertex AI Vizier hyperparameter or black-box optimization study, defining the parameter search space and objective metric its trial(s) are evaluated against.
google_aiplatform_tensorboard: `google_aiplatform_tensorboard` is a managed Vertex AI TensorBoard instance, the hosted service used to visualize training metrics (loss curves, scalars, embeddings) logged across one or more experiment runs.
google_aiplatform_time_sery: `google_aiplatform_time_sery` (a TimeSeries) is a single named sequence of scalar or tensor data points -- e.g. one training run's own loss curve -- logged to a Vertex AI TensorBoard for visualization.
google_aiplatform_training_pipeline: `google_aiplatform_training_pipeline` orchestrates the full path from a Vertex AI dataset to a trained, uploaded model in one managed step, wrapping AutoML or custom training plus any pre/post-processing around it.
google_aiplatform_trial: `google_aiplatform_trial` is a single parameter combination evaluated as part of a Vertex AI Vizier study or hyperparameter tuning job, recording the parameter values tried and the resulting objective metric value.
google_aiplatform_tuning_job: `google_aiplatform_tuning_job` fine-tunes a foundation model (e.g. a Gemini model) on Vertex AI using caller-supplied training data, producing a new, specialized tuned model version.
google_alloydb_backup: `google_alloydb_backup` is a point-in-time backup of an AlloyDB cluster, restorable to a new cluster.
google_alloydb_cluster: `google_alloydb_cluster` is the top-level AlloyDB resource, a PostgreSQL-compatible database cluster that primary and read pool instance(s) belong to.
google_alloydb_instance: `google_alloydb_instance` is a compute instance within an AlloyDB cluster -- either the primary read/write instance or a read pool instance serving read-only replica traffic.
google_alloydb_user: `google_alloydb_user` is a database user account on an AlloyDB cluster, authenticated via password or IAM.
google_apigee_aliase: `google_apigee_aliase` (an Alias) is a single named certificate or key entry stored inside an Apigee keystore or truststore, referenced by TLS configuration on a proxy or target endpoint.
google_apigee_api: `google_apigee_api` registers a standalone OpenAPI specification document with Apigee's own API hub/catalog, independent of any specific deployed proxy revision.
google_apigee_apicategory: `google_apigee_apicategory` defines a category label used to group and organize published API product(s) within an Apigee developer portal.
google_apigee_apidoc: `google_apigee_apidoc` publishes a single API's own reference documentation (an OpenAPI spec and supporting content) to an Apigee developer portal.
google_apigee_apim_service_extension: `google_apigee_apim_service_extension` wires Apigee's own API key and OAuth token verification into a Google Cloud load balancer via a service extension, enforcing Apigee policy on traffic without routing it through a full Apigee proxy.
google_apigee_apiproduct: `google_apigee_apiproduct` bundles one or more API proxy operations together into a single unit that developer apps request access to, the level access, quota, and rate limiting are configured at.
google_apigee_app: `google_apigee_app` (a Developer App) is the credential-holding registration a developer creates to consume one or more Apigee API products, carrying the API key(s) used to authenticate its own requests.
google_apigee_appgroup: `google_apigee_appgroup` groups multiple developer apps together under a single logical owner (e.g. a company or team) for API access management, an alternative to per-individual-developer app ownership.
google_apigee_archive_deployment: `google_apigee_archive_deployment` deploys a bundled archive of static configuration or resource file(s) to an Apigee environment, for use by proxy logic at runtime.
google_apigee_attachment: `google_apigee_attachment` attaches an Apigee environment group to a specific Apigee instance, controlling which runtime instance(s) actually serve traffic for that environment group's own hostnames.
google_apigee_canaryevaluation: `google_apigee_canaryevaluation` evaluates the real-time health impact of a runtime change rolled out to a small, canary subset of an Apigee instance's own message processors before Apigee decides whether to continue rolling it out further.
google_apigee_datacollector: `google_apigee_datacollector` defines a named, typed variable that Apigee proxy logic can write custom analytics data into, later queryable alongside Apigee's own built-in analytics dimensions.
google_apigee_datastore: `google_apigee_datastore` registers an external storage target (e.g. a Cloud Storage bucket or BigQuery dataset) Apigee analytics data or archived audit log export is written to.
google_apigee_debugsession: `google_apigee_debugsession` captures a short-lived, detailed trace of requests flowing through a deployed Apigee proxy revision, used to step through policy execution while diagnosing an issue.
google_apigee_developer: `google_apigee_developer` registers an individual, external API consumer with Apigee, the identity a developer app and its own API key(s) belong to.
google_apigee_dns_zone: `google_apigee_dns_zone` is a private DNS zone Apigee provisions for resolving hostnames within its own managed runtime instance network.
google_apigee_endpoint_attachment: `google_apigee_endpoint_attachment` establishes a Private Service Connect endpoint an Apigee proxy's own target endpoint can privately reach a backend service through, without traversing the public internet.
google_apigee_entry: `google_apigee_entry` is a single key/value pair stored inside an Apigee key-value map, read and written by proxy policy logic at runtime.
google_apigee_envgroup: `google_apigee_envgroup` (Environment Group) binds a set of hostnames to one or more Apigee environments, determining which environment's own deployed proxies handle traffic for a given incoming hostname.
google_apigee_environment: `google_apigee_environment` is a named runtime execution context (e.g. `test` or `prod`) within an Apigee organization that API proxies are deployed into, each with its own configuration and traffic isolation.
google_apigee_export: `google_apigee_export` runs a one-off job exporting an Apigee environment's own analytics data to Cloud Storage for external analysis.
google_apigee_host_query: `google_apigee_host_query` runs an asynchronous analytics query scoped across an entire Apigee organization's own runtime host, rather than a single environment.
google_apigee_host_security_report: `google_apigee_host_security_report` runs an asynchronous Advanced API Security report scoped across an entire Apigee organization's own runtime host.
google_apigee_instance: `google_apigee_instance` is a physical Apigee runtime deployment -- a set of message processors and routers provisioned in a specific region -- that environment(s) are attached to in order to actually serve API traffic.
google_apigee_key: `google_apigee_key` is the API key credential issued to a developer app, used to authenticate its own requests against Apigee-protected APIs.
google_apigee_keystore: `google_apigee_keystore` holds the TLS certificate and private key entries an Apigee proxy or target endpoint presents for inbound or outbound TLS connections.
google_apigee_keyvaluemap: `google_apigee_keyvaluemap` is a named, persistent key/value store Apigee proxy policy logic reads and writes at runtime, for caching or configuration data outside the proxy bundle itself.
google_apigee_nat_address: `google_apigee_nat_address` reserves a static outbound IP address an Apigee instance uses for NAT when its proxies make outbound calls to backend targets, so those targets can allowlist a known, stable source IP.
google_apigee_organization: `google_apigee_organization` is the top-level container for an entire Apigee deployment -- every environment, proxy, developer, and app a given Apigee account manages lives inside exactly one organization.
google_apigee_override: `google_apigee_override` overrides a specific check within an Apigee Advanced API Security security profile, excluding it from that profile's own assessment.
google_apigee_query: `google_apigee_query` runs an asynchronous analytics query against a single Apigee environment's own traffic data, for reporting scenarios too large for a synchronous request.
google_apigee_rateplan: `google_apigee_rateplan` defines the monetization pricing (per-transaction fees, revenue share, recurring charges) applied to a developer app's own usage of a monetized Apigee API product.
google_apigee_reference: `google_apigee_reference` is a named pointer inside an Apigee environment to another resource (e.g. a keystore), letting proxy configuration reference it indirectly so the underlying target can change without editing every proxy that uses it.
google_apigee_report: `google_apigee_report` defines a saved, reusable analytics report configuration (dimensions, metrics, filters) within an Apigee organization.
google_apigee_resourcefile: `google_apigee_resourcefile` is a supporting file (a JavaScript, XSLT, JSON schema, or similar script/config asset) bundled with an Apigee proxy or shared flow, referenced by its own policy steps.
google_apigee_security_action: `google_apigee_security_action` defines an automated response (allow, deny, or flag) Apigee Advanced API Security applies to traffic matching a specific condition, e.g. blocking requests from an IP address flagged as abusive.
google_apigee_security_feedback: `google_apigee_security_feedback` records a human reviewer's own correction to an Advanced API Security finding (e.g. marking a flagged IP address as a false positive), used to refine future detection.
google_apigee_security_monitoring_condit: `google_apigee_security_monitoring_condition` defines a condition Apigee Advanced API Security continuously monitors traffic against, triggering an alert or action when matched.
google_apigee_security_profile: `google_apigee_security_profile` is a named collection of Advanced API Security assessment checks that deployed proxies in an Apigee environment are evaluated against, producing a security score.
google_apigee_security_profiles_v2: `google_apigee_security_profiles_v2` is the current-generation Advanced API Security profile resource, the v2 API surface for the same security-profile assessment concept as `google_apigee_security_profile`.
google_apigee_security_report: `google_apigee_security_report` runs an asynchronous Advanced API Security analytics report against a single Apigee environment's own traffic data.
google_apigee_sharedflow: `google_apigee_sharedflow` packages a reusable sequence of Apigee policy steps that multiple different API proxies can invoke, avoiding duplicating the same policy logic across proxies.
google_apigee_space: `google_apigee_space` creates an identity-scoped isolation boundary within an Apigee organization, letting different teams manage their own proxies, products, and shared flows under separate IAM control without needing a fully separate organization.
google_apigee_subscription: `google_apigee_subscription` records a developer app's own active subscription to a monetized Apigee API product's rate plan.
google_apigee_targetserver: `google_apigee_targetserver` defines a named, reusable backend host (address, port, TLS config) an Apigee proxy's own target endpoint routes requests to, letting the actual backend be changed without editing every proxy that references it.
google_apihub_api: `google_apihub_api` registers a single API with API hub, Google Cloud's own catalog for discovering and governing every API across an organization, whether it runs on Google Cloud or elsewhere.
google_apihub_api_hub_instance: `google_apihub_api_hub_instance` is the provisioned API hub instance itself, the regional deployment new API, deployment, and plugin registration happens within.
google_apihub_attribute: `google_apihub_attribute` defines a custom metadata field (e.g. a maturity level or a team owner) that can be attached to APIs, versions, or other API hub entities for organization-specific classification.
google_apihub_curation: `google_apihub_curation` configures a plugin-driven job that automatically enriches or classifies discovered API metadata within API hub, e.g. auto-detecting an API's own maturity level.
google_apihub_dependency: `google_apihub_dependency` records a relationship between two entities cataloged in API hub, e.g. one API depending on another it calls internally.
google_apihub_deployment: `google_apihub_deployment` records where a specific API version is actually running (e.g. a specific API gateway or Apigee environment), linking the catalog entry to its real, live deployment.
google_apihub_external_api: `google_apihub_external_api` catalogs an API that isn't managed by Google Cloud at all (a third-party or partner API), so API hub's own discovery and dependency tracking covers it too.
google_apihub_host_project_registration: `google_apihub_host_project_registration` registers a Google Cloud project as a source API hub automatically discovers API deployments (e.g. Apigee proxies, API Gateway configs) from.
google_apihub_instance: `google_apihub_instance` is the provisioned API hub instance itself, the regional deployment new API, deployment, and plugin registration happens within.
google_apihub_operation: `google_apihub_operation` is a single documented operation (e.g. one REST endpoint or RPC method) belonging to an API version cataloged in API hub, parsed from its own spec.
google_apihub_plugin: `google_apihub_plugin` configures an integration that automatically discovers, curates, or enriches API metadata within API hub from an external or internal source.
google_apihub_runtime_project_attachment: `google_apihub_runtime_project_attachment` attaches a Google Cloud project as a source of runtime API traffic or deployment data that API hub ingests and links to its own catalog.
google_apihub_spec: `google_apihub_spec` is the actual specification document (OpenAPI, Protocol Buffers, or similar) uploaded for a specific API version cataloged in API hub.
google_apihub_version: `google_apihub_version` is a specific, named version of an API cataloged in API hub, grouping the spec, deployment(s), and operation(s) that belong to that version.
google_appengine_app: `google_appengine_app` is the single, per-project App Engine application resource -- once created, a project can have exactly one, and every App Engine service and version belongs to it.
google_appengine_authorized_certificate: `google_appengine_authorized_certificate` uploads a caller-managed SSL certificate for use with a custom domain mapped to an App Engine application.
google_appengine_domain_mapping: `google_appengine_domain_mapping` maps a custom domain to an App Engine application, routing that domain's own traffic to the app.
google_appengine_ingress_rule: `google_appengine_ingress_rule` restricts which source IP address range(s) are permitted to reach an App Engine application, part of its firewall configuration.
google_appengine_version: `google_appengine_version` is a specific, deployable version of an App Engine service, containing the actual application code and its own scaling and resource configuration.
google_apphub_application: `google_apphub_application` groups related service(s) and workload(s) together under a single logical application in App Hub, letting them be reasoned about and managed as one unit rather than individually.
google_apphub_service: `google_apphub_service` registers an underlying Google Cloud resource (e.g. a load balancer) as a discoverable network-facing service within an App Hub application.
google_apphub_service_project_attachment: `google_apphub_service_project_attachment` attaches a Google Cloud project as a source of discoverable service(s) and workload(s) that App Hub can register into an application.
google_apphub_workload: `google_apphub_workload` registers an underlying Google Cloud resource (e.g. a GKE deployment or Compute Engine instance group) as a discoverable compute workload within an App Hub application.
google_artifactregistry_attachment: `google_artifactregistry_attachment` associates supplementary metadata (e.g. an SBOM or a build attestation) with a specific artifact version stored in Artifact Registry.
google_artifactregistry_repository: `google_artifactregistry_repository` is an Artifact Registry repository, storing container image(s), language package(s), or other artifact(s) of a specific format.
google_artifactregistry_rule: `google_artifactregistry_rule` enforces a policy (e.g. an admission or immutability rule) on artifact(s) within an Artifact Registry repository.
google_artifactregistry_tag: `google_artifactregistry_tag` is a human-readable alias (e.g. `latest`) pointing at a specific version of an artifact stored in an Artifact Registry repository.
google_backupdr_backup_plan: `google_backupdr_backup_plan` defines the backup schedule and retention rule(s) Backup and DR applies to resource(s) it's associated with.
google_backupdr_backup_plan_association: `google_backupdr_backup_plan_association` attaches a specific workload (e.g. a Compute Engine VM) to a Backup and DR backup plan, activating scheduled backups for it.
google_backupdr_backup_vault: `google_backupdr_backup_vault` is the immutable, access-controlled storage container Backup and DR writes backup data into, protected against accidental or malicious deletion.
google_backupdr_management_server: `google_backupdr_management_server` is the central Backup and DR control-plane instance that manages backup plan(s), backup vault(s), and their own orchestration.
google_beyondcorp_app_connection: `google_beyondcorp_app_connection` defines a private application endpoint that BeyondCorp Enterprise's zero-trust remote access exposes to authorized users without a traditional VPN.
google_beyondcorp_app_connector: `google_beyondcorp_app_connector` is the agent deployed near a private application that establishes an outbound-only tunnel back to Google Cloud, so BeyondCorp Enterprise can reach it without inbound firewall rules.
google_beyondcorp_app_gateway: `google_beyondcorp_app_gateway` is the Google-managed ingress point that routes authorized user traffic from the internet through to a BeyondCorp Enterprise app connection.
google_beyondcorp_application: `google_beyondcorp_application` registers a private application under BeyondCorp Enterprise's own context-aware access policy, the resource IAM and access level(s) are granted against.
google_beyondcorp_security_gateway: `google_beyondcorp_security_gateway` is BeyondCorp Enterprise's own secure web gateway resource, applying zero-trust access policy to web traffic without requiring a per-app connector.
google_bigquery_dataset: `google_bigquery_dataset` is a BigQuery dataset, the top-level container that table(s), view(s), and routine(s) are organized within and IAM access is commonly granted at.
google_bigquery_job: `google_bigquery_job` is an asynchronous BigQuery operation -- a query, load, extract, or copy -- run against dataset(s) and table(s), tracked until it completes.
google_bigquery_routine: `google_bigquery_routine` is a saved, reusable BigQuery user-defined function or stored procedure, callable from SQL queries within its own dataset.
google_bigquery_row_access_policy: `google_bigquery_row_access_policy` restricts which row(s) of a BigQuery table a given principal can see, filtering query results based on the row's own data.
google_bigquery_table: `google_bigquery_table` is a BigQuery table (or view), the structured data resource queries are run against within a dataset.
google_bigtableadmin_app_profile: `google_bigtableadmin_app_profile` defines how a specific application connects to a Bigtable instance -- which cluster(s) it's routed to and the isolation guarantees it gets -- letting different apps sharing one instance be configured independently.
google_bigtableadmin_authorized_view: `google_bigtableadmin_authorized_view` restricts access to a defined subset of a Bigtable table's own rows and column families, letting IAM grant a caller visibility into only that subset rather than the whole table.
google_bigtableadmin_backup: `google_bigtableadmin_backup` is a point-in-time backup of a Bigtable table, restorable to a new table within the same instance or a different one.

google_bigtableadmin_schema_bundle: `google_bigtableadmin_schema_bundle` attaches Protocol Buffer schema definitions to a Bigtable table, letting stored `PROTO`-typed column values be interpreted with real field names and types instead of raw bytes.
google_bigtableadmin_table: `google_bigtableadmin_table` is a Bigtable table, the sparse, wide-column NoSQL structure that row data organized into column families is stored in.

google_certificatemanager_trust_config: `google_certificatemanager_trust_config` defines a set of trusted root and intermediate CA certificates Certificate Manager uses to validate client certificates during mutual TLS.
google_ces_agent: `google_ces_agent` is a conversational agent built with Customer Engagement Suite's own CX Agent Studio, the underlying generative agent an app is configured to run.
google_ces_app: `google_ces_app` is a deployable customer engagement application in Customer Engagement Suite (CX Agent Studio), packaging an agent along with its own guardrails and deployment settings.

google_ces_toolset: `google_ces_toolset` groups related tool(s) together for a Customer Engagement Suite agent, letting a set of capabilities be attached and managed together.
google_ces_version: `google_ces_version` is an immutable, point-in-time snapshot of a Customer Engagement Suite app, created when a deployment is published.
google_clouddeploy_automation: `google_clouddeploy_automation` configures Cloud Deploy to automatically run action(s) (e.g. promoting a release to the next stage, or repeating a rollout) when a defined event occurs in a delivery pipeline, without a human triggering it.
google_clouddeploy_custom_target_type: `google_clouddeploy_custom_target_type` defines a Cloud Deploy target type for a deployment destination not natively supported (e.g. a custom Kubernetes operator or a non-Google runtime), via a caller-supplied Skaffold custom action.
google_clouddeploy_delivery_pipeline: `google_clouddeploy_delivery_pipeline` defines the ordered sequence of target(s) (e.g. dev, staging, prod) a Cloud Deploy release progressively rolls out through.
google_clouddeploy_deploy_policy: `google_clouddeploy_deploy_policy` restricts when and how Cloud Deploy rollouts are permitted to run against a target, e.g. blocking deployments outside an approved change window.
google_clouddeploy_release: `google_clouddeploy_release` is a specific, immutable set of application artifacts (rendered from a delivery pipeline's own configuration) that Cloud Deploy progressively rolls out across a pipeline's own target(s).
google_clouddeploy_rollout: `google_clouddeploy_rollout` is the actual deployment of a Cloud Deploy release to one specific target in the delivery pipeline, the unit that succeeds, fails, or is rolled back.
google_clouddeploy_target: `google_clouddeploy_target` defines a single deployment destination (a GKE cluster, Cloud Run service, or custom target) a Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline can roll out a release to.
google_cloudidentity_allowlisted_domain: `google_cloudidentity_allowlisted_domain` permits a specific external Cloud Identity domain to have its own users provisioned or referenced (e.g. as group members) from within the calling organization.
google_cloudidentity_device: `google_cloudidentity_device` represents an end-user device (a phone, laptop) enrolled in Cloud Identity's own device management, tracked for compliance and access-control purposes.
google_cloudidentity_group: `google_cloudidentity_group` is a Cloud Identity group -- a named collection of member(s), used for email distribution, access control, or organizational structure across Google Workspace and Google Cloud.
google_cloudidentity_inbound_oidc_sso_pr: `google_cloudidentity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile` configures Cloud Identity to accept single sign-on from an external OpenID Connect identity provider, letting users authenticate with their own third-party IdP credentials.
google_cloudidentity_inbound_saml_sso_pr: `google_cloudidentity_inbound_saml_sso_profile` configures Cloud Identity to accept single sign-on from an external SAML identity provider, letting users authenticate with their own third-party IdP credentials.
google_cloudidentity_inbound_sso_assignm: `google_cloudidentity_inbound_sso_assignment` assigns a specific group or org unit of Cloud Identity users to authenticate through a particular configured inbound SSO profile.
google_cloudidentity_membership: `google_cloudidentity_membership` adds a user, group, or service account as a member of a Cloud Identity group, with a specified role (owner, manager, or member).
google_cloudidentity_policy: `google_cloudidentity_policy` defines a Cloud Identity administrative policy (e.g. a group creation or membership restriction) applied across an organization or a specific org unit.

google_cloudkms_key_ring: `google_cloudkms_key_ring` is a regional grouping of Cloud KMS crypto key(s), the container keys are organized under and IAM access is commonly granted at.
google_cloudkms_proposal: `google_cloudkms_proposal` is a quorum-based, time-limited request for a sensitive Single-tenant Cloud HSM operation (e.g. registering a new control key), which must be approved by enough administrators signing with their own control keys before it can run.
google_cloudkms_single_tenant_hsm_instan: `google_cloudkms_single_tenant_hsm_instance` provisions a dedicated, single-tenant Cloud HSM cluster with quorum-based administrative control, for workloads that require exclusive, non-shared hardware security module capacity.
google_cloudresourcemanager_folder: `google_cloudresourcemanager_folder` groups project(s) and other folder(s) together in the Google Cloud resource hierarchy, letting IAM policy and organization policy be applied to the whole group at once.
google_cloudresourcemanager_lien: `google_cloudresourcemanager_lien` blocks a Google Cloud project from being deleted until the lien is explicitly removed, a safeguard against accidental deletion of a project something else depends on.
google_cloudresourcemanager_project: `google_cloudresourcemanager_project` is a Google Cloud project, the base-level container that billing, IAM policy, and every other resource in this system are ultimately scoped under.
google_cloudresourcemanager_tag_key: `google_cloudresourcemanager_tag_key` defines a named key (e.g. `environment`) for Google Cloud resource tags, that specific tag value(s) are created underneath and attached to resources for organization policy and access-control targeting.
google_cloudresourcemanager_tag_value: `google_cloudresourcemanager_tag_value` defines a specific permitted value (e.g. `production`) under a resource tag key, that can be attached to resources and referenced by conditional IAM bindings or organization policy.
google_compute_address: `google_compute_address` reserves a static external IP address in a region, so a resource that needs a stable, known address (rather than one that changes on every restart) can be assigned one explicitly.
google_compute_autoscaler: `google_compute_autoscaler` adjusts a zonal managed instance group's own size automatically based on real load -- CPU utilization, a custom metric, load balancing capacity -- adding instances under pressure and removing them once it passes.
google_compute_backend_bucket: `google_compute_backend_bucket` lets a global HTTP(S) load balancer serve real content directly out of a Cloud Storage bucket, for the parts of a site (static assets, media) that don't need a real backend server behind them at all.
google_compute_backend_service: `google_compute_backend_service` defines how a load balancer actually distributes real traffic across a set of backends -- instance groups, network endpoint groups, buckets -- including the health check, timeout, and session affinity settings that govern that distribution.
google_compute_cross_site_network: `google_compute_cross_site_network` groups the real Cross-Site Interconnect connections used to link two of your own physical sites directly through Google's network, rather than routing that private, site-to-site traffic over the public internet.
google_compute_disk: `google_compute_disk` is a zonal persistent block storage volume attached to a Compute Engine instance -- the real, durable storage a VM's own root filesystem or extra data volumes actually live on, independent of the instance's own lifecycle.
google_compute_external_vpn_gateway: `google_compute_external_vpn_gateway` represents the real, non-Google side of a VPN tunnel -- the on-premises or other-cloud VPN device Cloud VPN connects to, described here so Google's own side knows where to route encrypted traffic.
google_compute_firewall: `google_compute_firewall` allows or denies real traffic to and from instances in a VPC network, matched by direction, protocol, port, and source or destination -- the real, network-level access control every instance in the network is subject to.
google_compute_firewall_policy: `google_compute_firewall_policy` is a real, reusable set of firewall rules that can be attached to a VPC network -- unlike a plain firewall rule, a policy's own rules can be shared across multiple networks and evaluated together with a defined priority order.
google_compute_forwarding_rule: `google_compute_forwarding_rule` directs real traffic arriving at a specific IP address and port to the actual load balancer or target resource meant to handle it -- the entry point every Google Cloud load balancer type is built around.
google_compute_future_reservation: `google_compute_future_reservation` requests real compute capacity -- a specific VM size, GPU, or TPU -- to become available starting on a date up to a year out, so high-demand hardware is guaranteed to actually be there when a real, planned workload needs it.
google_compute_global_address: `google_compute_global_address` reserves a static external IP address usable by a global resource, like a global load balancer, rather than being scoped to a single region the way a regional address is.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule: `google_compute_global_forwarding_rule` is the global counterpart to a forwarding rule -- directing real traffic arriving at a global IP address to a global load balancer, used when the backend itself is spread across multiple regions.
google_compute_global_network_endpoint_g: `google_compute_global_network_endpoint_group` groups real network endpoints -- often an external, non-Google backend reachable by IP or FQDN -- that a global load balancer can route to, the mechanism for load balancing to endpoints outside Google Cloud entirely.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p: `google_compute_global_public_delegated_prefix` delegates a real, global block of your own public IP addresses to Google Cloud to advertise and manage on your behalf, rather than using addresses Google itself owns.
google_compute_global_vm_extension_polic: `google_compute_global_vm_extension_policy` declares which VM extensions -- agents and other post-boot software -- VM Extension Manager should install across every matching VM in a project, across every zone and region at once rather than one location at a time.
google_compute_health_check: `google_compute_health_check` defines how a load balancer or managed instance group actually determines whether a backend instance is healthy -- the protocol, the port, how often to check, and how many failures before it's marked unhealthy and taken out of rotation.
google_compute_http_health_check: `google_compute_http_health_check` is the original, legacy HTTP health check type used specifically by target pools and network load balancers -- superseded for newer load balancer types by the general, protocol-agnostic health check resource, but still real, live API surface for the older ones.
google_compute_https_health_check: `google_compute_https_health_check` is the legacy HTTPS counterpart to the original HTTP health check, used the same way by target pools and network load balancers rather than the newer, general health check resource.
google_compute_image: `google_compute_image` is a real, reusable boot disk image -- a public OS image, or one you've captured yourself -- used as the real starting point for creating new Compute Engine instances or disks.
google_compute_instance: `google_compute_instance` is a real, running virtual machine in Compute Engine -- its machine type, boot disk, network interfaces, and metadata all defined here, the core compute resource everything else in this reference ultimately supports.
google_compute_instance_group: `google_compute_instance_group` is an unmanaged collection of existing instances grouped together so they can be referenced as one unit -- by a load balancer, for instance -- without Compute Engine automatically creating, healing, or scaling any of them the way a managed instance group does.

google_compute_instance_template: `google_compute_instance_template` is a real, reusable specification for creating instances -- machine type, boot disk, network settings -- that a managed instance group uses to stamp out every instance in the group identically.
google_compute_instant_snapshot: `google_compute_instant_snapshot` is a real, near-instantaneous, zonal point-in-time copy of a persistent disk -- faster to create and restore from than a standard snapshot, at the cost of needing to stay in the same zone as the disk it came from.
google_compute_instant_snapshot_group: `google_compute_instant_snapshot_group` captures a real, consistent instant snapshot across multiple disks at once -- for a VM with several attached disks that all need to be captured at exactly the same moment to actually be restorable together.
google_compute_interconnect: `google_compute_interconnect` represents a real, physical connection between your own network and Google's network at a real colocation facility -- the dedicated, private link Cloud Interconnect is actually built on top of.

google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g: `google_compute_interconnect_attachment_group` groups multiple real interconnect attachments together so their combined availability and configuration can be managed and monitored as one real unit rather than individually.
google_compute_interconnect_group: `google_compute_interconnect_group` groups multiple real Interconnect connections together -- typically for redundancy across different physical facilities -- so their combined resilience can be validated and monitored as a real, single unit.
google_compute_license: `google_compute_license` tracks the real licensing terms and restrictions attached to an image or disk -- the mechanism behind bring-your-own-license and marketplace image billing, not something a user typically creates directly.
google_compute_machine_image: `google_compute_machine_image` captures a real, complete instance -- boot disk, any additional disks, and its own instance configuration -- as one reusable artifact, unlike a plain image which only captures the boot disk.
google_compute_network: `google_compute_network` is a real Virtual Private Cloud network -- a global, software-defined network that a project's own subnets, firewall rules, and routes all live inside, the top-level container every other real networking resource here is scoped underneath.
google_compute_network_attachment: `google_compute_network_attachment` lets another VPC network connect into your own network via Private Service Connect, without you having to know or manage that other network's own IP ranges -- the producer-side resource a real, cross-project PSC connection is built on.
google_compute_network_edge_security_ser: `google_compute_network_edge_security_service` enables advanced network DDoS protection for every applicable regional resource -- network load balancers, protocol forwarding, VMs with public IPs -- in one region at once, by attaching a Cloud Armor network security policy to it.
google_compute_network_endpoint_group: `google_compute_network_endpoint_group` groups real backend endpoints a load balancer can route to -- individual VM IP:port pairs, serverless services, or endpoints outside Google Cloud -- a more granular real target than pointing a load balancer at a whole instance group.
google_compute_network_firewall_policy: `google_compute_network_firewall_policy` is a global, real, reusable set of firewall rules attachable to a VPC network -- the network-scoped counterpart to a hierarchical (organization/folder-level) firewall policy.
google_compute_node_group: `google_compute_node_group` is a real collection of sole-tenant nodes -- physical servers dedicated entirely to your own project -- that VMs can be placed onto for real, dedicated hardware isolation.
google_compute_node_template: `google_compute_node_template` defines the real hardware specification -- node type, CPU overcommit settings -- that a sole-tenant node group uses to actually provision the physical nodes inside it.
google_compute_organization_security_pol: `google_compute_organization_security_policy` is a real, hierarchical firewall policy enforceable across an entire organization or folder -- rules set here can't be overridden by a lower-level policy, giving organization-wide admins one real place to manage critical, non-negotiable firewall rules.
google_compute_packet_mirroring: `google_compute_packet_mirroring` clones real network traffic to and from a set of instances and sends the copy to a collector, without disrupting the original traffic at all -- used for real, out-of-band security monitoring and intrusion detection.
google_compute_public_advertised_prefix: `google_compute_public_advertised_prefix` registers a real, top-level block of your own public IP addresses with Google, the first real step before any smaller delegated prefix carved out of it can be used on Google Cloud.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefix: `google_compute_public_delegated_prefix` carves a real, smaller, regional block of addresses out of an already-registered public advertised prefix, delegating that specific slice for actual use within one region.

google_compute_region_backend_bucket: `google_compute_region_backend_bucket` is the regional counterpart to a global backend bucket, letting a regional load balancer serve content directly from Cloud Storage.
google_compute_region_backend_service: `google_compute_region_backend_service` is the regional counterpart to a global backend service -- the same real health check, timeout, and traffic distribution configuration, scoped to backends within one region for a regional load balancer.
google_compute_region_commitment: `google_compute_region_commitment` is a regional committed-use discount -- a real, one- or three-year commitment to a specific amount of vCPU, memory, or GPU usage in one region, in exchange for a lower real hourly rate than on-demand pricing.
google_compute_region_composite_health_c: `google_compute_region_composite_health_check` combines the real health states of multiple individual health sources into one overall health verdict for a regional published service -- the service counts as healthy only when enough of its own real health sources agree it is.
google_compute_region_disk: `google_compute_region_disk` is a persistent disk replicated synchronously across two zones in a region, rather than living in just one zone -- real protection against a single zone failure, at the cost of the extra real replication overhead.
google_compute_region_health_aggregation: `google_compute_region_health_aggregation_policy` defines the real conditions -- a minimum percentage of healthy backends, a minimum count -- that a composite health check actually applies when deciding whether a regional published service as a whole should be considered healthy.
google_compute_region_health_check: `google_compute_region_health_check` is the regional counterpart to a global health check, used by regional load balancers and regional managed instance groups to determine real backend health within that one region.
google_compute_region_health_check_servi: `google_compute_region_health_check_service` is the regional configuration tying a health check to the real notification endpoints that should be told when a monitored resource's own health status actually changes.
google_compute_region_health_source: `google_compute_region_health_source` is one real, individual input a composite health check combines with others -- a Private Service Connect endpoint's own health, for instance -- into that composite check's single, overall health verdict.

google_compute_region_instant_snapshot: `google_compute_region_instant_snapshot` is the regional counterpart to a zonal instant snapshot -- a fast, point-in-time copy of a regional (multi-zone replicated) persistent disk.
google_compute_region_instant_snapshot_g: `google_compute_region_instant_snapshot_group` is the regional counterpart to a zonal instant snapshot group, capturing a consistent, real snapshot across multiple regional disks at once.
google_compute_region_network_endpoint_g: `google_compute_region_network_endpoint_group` is the regional counterpart to a global network endpoint group -- grouping real backend endpoints within one region for a regional load balancer to route to, including serverless (Cloud Run, App Engine) backends specifically.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p: `google_compute_region_network_firewall_policy` is the regional counterpart to a global network firewall policy -- a real, reusable rule set attachable to networks, scoped to a single region.
google_compute_region_notification_endpo: `google_compute_region_notification_endpoint` is the regional counterpart to a global notification endpoint -- receiving real status-change notifications from a regional health check service the moment a monitored resource's own health changes.
google_compute_region_security_policy: `google_compute_region_security_policy` is the regional counterpart to a global Cloud Armor security policy, applied to backends behind a regional, rather than global, load balancer.
google_compute_region_snapshot: `google_compute_region_snapshot` is the regional counterpart to a standard, multi-region snapshot -- a real, durable, point-in-time disk backup stored specifically within one region rather than replicated more broadly.
google_compute_region_ssl_certificate: `google_compute_region_ssl_certificate` is the regional counterpart to a global SSL certificate, usable by a regional HTTPS or SSL proxy load balancer to actually terminate TLS.
google_compute_region_ssl_policy: `google_compute_region_ssl_policy` is the regional counterpart to a global SSL policy, controlling which real TLS versions and cipher suites a regional load balancer accepts.
google_compute_region_target_http_proxy: `google_compute_region_target_http_proxy` is the regional counterpart to a global target HTTP proxy -- routing real, unencrypted HTTP traffic to a backend service via a regional URL map.

google_compute_region_target_tcp_proxy: `google_compute_region_target_tcp_proxy` is the regional counterpart to a global target TCP proxy, routing real TCP traffic to a backend service scoped to one region.
google_compute_region_url_map: `google_compute_region_url_map` is the regional counterpart to a global URL map -- the real, host- and path-based routing rules a regional HTTP(S) load balancer uses to decide which backend service handles a given request.
google_compute_reservation: `google_compute_reservation` sets aside real compute capacity -- a specific machine type and count, in a specific zone -- guaranteeing it's actually available for your own VMs to consume, rather than competing for capacity with every other customer at boot time.
google_compute_resource_policy: `google_compute_resource_policy` is a real, reusable schedule attachable to disks or instances -- automated snapshot creation, or a real start/stop schedule for an instance -- defined once and applied to many resources rather than scripted separately for each.

google_compute_security_policy: `google_compute_security_policy` is a Cloud Armor policy -- real WAF rules, rate limiting, and DDoS protection -- attached to a backend service to filter traffic before it ever reaches a real backend.
