google_compute_vpn_gateway: `google_compute_vpn_gateway` represents the modern, HA VPN version of Google's own side of a VPN connection -- built for real 99.99% availability via redundant real interfaces, the replacement for the older Classic target VPN gateway.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel: `google_compute_vpn_tunnel` is one real, encrypted IPsec tunnel between a Google VPN gateway and an external peer -- the actual, active connection real traffic flows through once a VPN gateway is set up.
google_compute_wire_group: `google_compute_wire_group` configures real bandwidth and traffic settings on top of a Cross-Site Interconnect connection -- VLAN or port mode, unmetered bandwidth, optional MACsec encryption -- the resource that actually carries traffic across a cross-site network.
google_compute_zone_vm_extension_policy: `google_compute_zone_vm_extension_policy` is the zonal counterpart to a global VM extension policy -- declaring which extensions VM Extension Manager should install on matching VMs within one specific zone rather than across every zone and region at once.
google_contactcenterinsights_analyse: `google_contactcenterinsights_analyse` (an Analysis) runs Contact Center AI Insights' own ML-based processing over a single conversation, producing sentiment, entity, intent, and issue detection results.
google_contactcenterinsights_analysis_ru: `google_contactcenterinsights_analysis_rule` automatically triggers a Contact Center AI Insights analysis on conversation(s) matching a defined filter, instead of requiring each analysis to be requested manually.
google_contactcenterinsights_assessment: `google_contactcenterinsights_assessment` records a completed quality assurance evaluation of a conversation against a scorecard, holding the scored answer(s) to each of the scorecard's own question(s).
google_contactcenterinsights_assessment_: `google_contactcenterinsights_assessment_rule` automatically assigns quality assurance assessment(s) to conversation(s) matching a defined filter, for scheduled or sampled agent review.
google_contactcenterinsights_assistant_s: `google_contactcenterinsights_assistant_session` is a single live session of Conversational Insights' own real-time Agent Assist, providing an active human agent with suggested response(s) and information while a conversation is in progress.
google_contactcenterinsights_authorized_: `google_contactcenterinsights_authorized_view` restricts a principal's own access within Contact Center AI Insights to a defined subset of conversation data, for role-based data isolation.
`google_contactcenterinsights_authorized_view_set` groups related authorized views together for easier bulk assignment of the same data-access scope to multiple principals.
google_contactcenterinsights_auto_labeli: `google_contactcenterinsights_auto_labeling_rule` automatically assigns a feedback label to conversation(s) matching a defined condition, building a labeled dataset without manual tagging.
google_contactcenterinsights_chart: `google_contactcenterinsights_chart` defines a single visualization (e.g. a trend line or breakdown) displayed on a Contact Center AI Insights dashboard.
google_contactcenterinsights_conversatio: `google_contactcenterinsights_conversation` is a single imported customer interaction (a call transcript or chat log) that Contact Center AI Insights analyzes for sentiment, topics, and quality signals.
google_contactcenterinsights_dashboard: `google_contactcenterinsights_dashboard` is a saved collection of chart(s) presenting Contact Center AI Insights analytics, e.g. call volume or sentiment trends over time.
google_contactcenterinsights_dataset: `google_contactcenterinsights_dataset` is a named collection of conversation(s) grouped together in Contact Center AI Insights, e.g. for training an issue model or running a bulk analysis.
google_contactcenterinsights_feedback_la: `google_contactcenterinsights_feedback_label` records a human-assigned ground-truth label on a conversation, used to evaluate and improve Contact Center AI Insights' own model accuracy.
google_contactcenterinsights_issue: `google_contactcenterinsights_issue` is a single, automatically discovered topic or theme (e.g. `billing dispute`) within a Contact Center AI Insights issue model, that conversations are classified against.
google_contactcenterinsights_issue_model: `google_contactcenterinsights_issue_model` trains an ML model over a set of conversations to automatically discover and classify the recurring issue(s) customers are calling about.
google_contactcenterinsights_phrase_matc: `google_contactcenterinsights_phrase_matcher` defines a rule matching specific phrase(s) or pattern(s) spoken during a conversation, flagging matching conversations for Contact Center AI Insights' own analysis.
google_contactcenterinsights_qa_question: `google_contactcenterinsights_qa_question` defines a single quality-assurance question (e.g. `Did the agent greet the customer?`) within a QA scorecard, either scored manually or automatically.
`google_contactcenterinsights_qa_question_tag` is a label applied to a QA scorecard question, used to group and filter question(s) across scorecards.
google_contactcenterinsights_qa_scorecar: `google_contactcenterinsights_qa_scorecard` defines the set of quality-assurance question(s) used to grade a customer service conversation's own handling.
google_contactcenterinsights_revision: `google_contactcenterinsights_revision` is a saved, versioned snapshot of a QA scorecard's own question set, letting past assessments remain tied to the exact scorecard version they were scored against.
google_contactcenterinsights_view: `google_contactcenterinsights_view` defines a saved, reusable filter over Contact Center AI Insights conversation data, used to scope dashboards, exports, or bulk analysis to a specific subset.
google_datacatalog_entry: `google_datacatalog_entry` is a single cataloged item in Data Catalog -- a table, file set, or other real or logical asset -- carrying its own searchable metadata and tag(s).
google_datacatalog_entry_group: `google_datacatalog_entry_group` is a logical container of related entries within Data Catalog, typically grouping entries that share the same source system.
google_datacatalog_policy_tag: `google_datacatalog_policy_tag` defines a data classification node within a Data Catalog policy tag taxonomy, used to enforce BigQuery column-level access control based on sensitivity.
google_datacatalog_tag_template: `google_datacatalog_tag_template` defines the schema (field names and types) for a reusable kind of tag that can be attached to Data Catalog entries, e.g. a `data_governance` tag with an `owner` field.
google_datacatalog_taxonomy: `google_datacatalog_taxonomy` is a hierarchical classification scheme (a tree of policy tag nodes) Data Catalog uses to tag data with sensitivity or business categories for governance.
google_dataform_compilation_result: `google_dataform_compilation_result` is the compiled output of a Dataform repository's own SQLX source code at a specific commit, resolving all references and configuration into the actual executable SQL graph a workflow invocation runs.
google_dataform_folder: `google_dataform_folder` organizes code asset(s) (repositories holding SQLX transformations, notebooks, saved queries) into a hierarchical structure within Dataform, similar to folders in a file system.
google_dataform_release_config: `google_dataform_release_config` schedules Dataform to automatically compile a repository's own code from a specific Git reference on a recurring basis, producing a fresh compilation result ready for workflow execution.
google_dataform_repository: `google_dataform_repository` is a single Git-backed Dataform repository containing one code asset -- typically a set of SQLX data transformation definitions, but also a notebook, saved query, or similar asset.
google_dataform_team_folder: `google_dataform_team_folder` is a shared-drive-like Dataform folder designed for team collaboration on code assets, distinct from a personal folder scoped to a single user.
google_dataform_workflow_config: `google_dataform_workflow_config` schedules a Dataform workflow invocation to run automatically on a recurring basis against a specific compilation result.
google_dataform_workflow_invocation: `google_dataform_workflow_invocation` is a single execution of a Dataform compilation result's own SQL graph, running the data transformation(s) it defines against the target data warehouse.
google_dataform_workspace: `google_dataform_workspace` is a personal, uncommitted development workspace within a Dataform repository, where a developer edits SQLX code before pushing it to the shared Git history.
google_dataplex_aspect_type: `google_dataplex_aspect_type` defines a reusable, structured schema for a business or technical metadata facet (e.g. a data quality score or a PII classification) that can be attached to any Dataplex catalog entry as an aspect.
google_dataplex_asset: `google_dataplex_asset` registers an underlying data source -- a Cloud Storage bucket or BigQuery dataset -- with a Dataplex zone, bringing it under that zone's own governance and discovery.
google_dataplex_attribute: `google_dataplex_attribute` defines a single node in a Dataplex data taxonomy's own classification hierarchy, e.g. a sensitivity level like `Confidential`.
google_dataplex_binding: `google_dataplex_binding` grants IAM role(s) to principal(s) scoped to a specific set of resources within Dataplex Universal Catalog (rebranded Knowledge Catalog as of April 2026), narrower than a project-level IAM binding.
google_dataplex_category: `google_dataplex_category` defines a data classification node within a Dataplex policy tag taxonomy, used to enforce BigQuery column-level access control based on sensitivity.
google_dataplex_data_asset: `google_dataplex_data_asset` is a curated data asset packaged as part of a Dataplex Data Product -- one of the underlying dataset(s), table(s), or view(s) that make up a governed, business-ready data offering.
google_dataplex_data_attribute_binding: `google_dataplex_data_attribute_binding` attaches a data taxonomy attribute (e.g. a sensitivity classification) to a specific data asset, resource, or column within Dataplex.
google_dataplex_data_domain: `google_dataplex_data_domain` groups related data product(s) and their own governance ownership under a single business domain (e.g. `Finance` or `Marketing`) within Dataplex's data mesh model.
google_dataplex_data_product: `google_dataplex_data_product` is a curated, business-ready package of data asset(s), documentation, quality contracts, and governance controls assembled in Dataplex to solve a specific business problem, the unit Dataplex's data mesh capability is organized around.
google_dataplex_data_scan: `google_dataplex_data_scan` runs an automated data quality or data profiling scan against a BigQuery table or Cloud Storage dataset, producing rule-level pass/fail results and column-level statistics.
google_dataplex_data_taxonomy: `google_dataplex_data_taxonomy` is a hierarchical classification scheme (a tree of attribute nodes) Dataplex uses to tag data with sensitivity or business categories for governance.
google_dataplex_encryption_config: `google_dataplex_encryption_config` configures a customer-managed encryption key for Dataplex to use when encrypting a lake's own managed resources.
google_dataplex_entity: `google_dataplex_entity` registers a single structured or semi-structured data entity (a table-like object backed by files or a BigQuery table) discovered or defined within a Dataplex zone.
google_dataplex_entry: `google_dataplex_entry` is a single cataloged item in Dataplex Universal Catalog (Knowledge Catalog) -- a table, file set, dashboard, or any other real or logical asset -- carrying its own metadata and aspect(s).
google_dataplex_entry_group: `google_dataplex_entry_group` is a logical container of related catalog entries within Dataplex Universal Catalog, typically grouping entries that share the same source system or namespace.
google_dataplex_entry_link: `google_dataplex_entry_link` defines a typed relationship between two Dataplex catalog entries, e.g. connecting a business glossary term to the specific table column it defines.
google_dataplex_entry_type: `google_dataplex_entry_type` defines the schema (which aspect types are required or allowed) that catalog entries of a given kind must conform to in Dataplex Universal Catalog.
google_dataplex_glossary: `google_dataplex_glossary` is a business glossary in Dataplex Universal Catalog -- a hierarchical structure of business term(s) and category/categories that can be linked to real catalog entries for shared, governed terminology.
google_dataplex_lake: `google_dataplex_lake` is the top-level organizational container in Dataplex, grouping related zone(s) and their own underlying data assets under one logical data lake.
google_dataplex_metadata_feed: `google_dataplex_metadata_feed` triggers automatic Dataplex Catalog entry updates whenever a linked resource's own metadata (e.g. a BigQuery table's schema) changes.
google_dataplex_metadata_job: `google_dataplex_metadata_job` runs a bulk import or export operation against Dataplex Universal Catalog metadata, e.g. bulk-creating entries, aspects, or glossary term links from an external source.
google_dataplex_partition: `google_dataplex_partition` registers a single partition (e.g. one date-sharded slice) of a Dataplex entity's own underlying data.
google_dataplex_task: `google_dataplex_task` schedules a recurring or one-off Spark job (a notebook or custom script) to run against data managed within a Dataplex lake.
google_dataplex_term: `google_dataplex_term` is a single business term defined within a Dataplex Universal Catalog glossary, e.g. a shared definition of `Customer Lifetime Value`.
google_dataplex_zone: `google_dataplex_zone` subdivides a Dataplex lake into a raw or curated area, each with its own data-management policy, that asset(s) are attached to.
google_dataproc_autoscaling_policy: `google_dataproc_autoscaling_policy` defines rules for automatically resizing a Dataproc cluster's own worker node count in response to YARN pending-memory pressure.
google_dataproc_batch: `google_dataproc_batch` runs a single Spark, PySpark, or SparkR workload on serverless Dataproc, without the caller having to provision or manage a persistent cluster.
google_dataproc_cluster: `google_dataproc_cluster` is a managed Hadoop/Spark cluster, the persistent compute resource Dataproc jobs are submitted to run on.
google_dataproc_node_group: `google_dataproc_node_group` defines a named group of additional worker node(s) within a Dataproc cluster, e.g. a set of preemptible/Spot nodes distinct from the cluster's own primary workers.
google_dataproc_session: `google_dataproc_session` is an interactive, serverless Spark session on Dataproc, letting a notebook or client run multiple Spark statements against shared, live compute without a persistent cluster.
google_dataproc_session_template: `google_dataproc_session_template` defines a reusable configuration (runtime version, resource sizing) new Dataproc interactive sessions can be created from.
google_dataproc_workflow_template: `google_dataproc_workflow_template` defines a reusable, ordered graph of Dataproc job(s) (with dependencies between them) that can be instantiated and run as a single managed workflow.
google_datastream_connection_profile: `google_datastream_connection_profile` defines the connectivity and credentials Datastream uses to reach a specific source or destination database or storage system.
google_datastream_private_connection: `google_datastream_private_connection` establishes private connectivity (via VPC peering) between Datastream and a source database that isn't reachable over the public internet.
google_datastream_route: `google_datastream_route` defines a network route within a Datastream private connection, letting traffic reach source database(s) on an overlapping or non-default IP range.
google_datastream_stream: `google_datastream_stream` is a Datastream change-data-capture pipeline that continuously replicates data from a source connection profile to a destination.
google_developerconnect_account_connecto: `google_developerconnect_account_connector` links a Google Cloud project to a developer's own OAuth-authorized account on an external platform (e.g. GitHub), the credential Developer Connect connections are created under.
google_developerconnect_connection: `google_developerconnect_connection` establishes a Developer Connect link to a third-party source code platform (GitHub, GitLab, and similar), the resource git repository links are created under.
google_developerconnect_git_repository_l: `google_developerconnect_git_repository_link` links a specific external Git repository into Google Cloud through a Developer Connect connection, enabling CI/CD and AI-assisted development integrations against it.
google_developerconnect_insights_config: `google_developerconnect_insights_config` enables Developer Connect Insights (Application Insights) for a linked repository, automatically discovering the application(s) and runtime deployment(s) built from its own code.
google_dialogflow_agent: `google_dialogflow_agent` is the top-level Dialogflow CX (Conversational Agents) virtual agent, the container holding every flow, playbook, entity type, and other configuration that defines how it converses with users.
google_dialogflow_entity_type: `google_dialogflow_entity_type` defines a category of value (e.g. a city name or product SKU) a Dialogflow agent can extract from user input, along with its own synonyms and matching behavior.
google_dialogflow_environment: `google_dialogflow_environment` is a deployable environment (e.g. `staging` or `production`) that a specific, pinned version of a Dialogflow agent runs in, letting changes be tested before going live.
google_dialogflow_example: `google_dialogflow_example` is a sample conversation used to few-shot guide a Dialogflow CX generative playbook's own behavior, showing the model an example of the desired input/output pattern.
google_dialogflow_experiment: `google_dialogflow_experiment` runs an A/B test between two versions of a Dialogflow agent's own flow, routing a portion of live traffic to the variant to measure which performs better.
google_dialogflow_flow: `google_dialogflow_flow` is a self-contained conversational module (a directed graph of page(s) and transition(s)) within a Dialogflow CX agent, typically handling one topic or task.
google_dialogflow_generator: `google_dialogflow_generator` defines a reusable LLM prompt template a Dialogflow CX agent invokes mid-conversation to generate dynamic content, e.g. a summary or a suggested response.
google_dialogflow_intent: `google_dialogflow_intent` maps a category of user input (defined by training phrases) to a specific meaning a Dialogflow agent should recognize and act on.
google_dialogflow_page: `google_dialogflow_page` is a single conversational state within a Dialogflow CX flow, defining what the agent says and which transition(s) it evaluates based on user input while in that state.
google_dialogflow_playbook: `google_dialogflow_playbook` defines a Dialogflow CX agent's own conversational behavior using natural-language instructions and goals for an LLM to follow, the generative alternative to hand-built flow/page state machines.
google_dialogflow_security_setting: `google_dialogflow_security_setting` configures data retention, redaction, and storage location policy for a Dialogflow agent's own conversation data.
google_dialogflow_test_case: `google_dialogflow_test_case` defines a scripted conversation with expected agent response(s), used to automatically verify a Dialogflow agent's own behavior hasn't regressed after a change.
google_dialogflow_tool: `google_dialogflow_tool` registers an external function, API, or data store a Dialogflow CX playbook can call during a conversation to fetch information or take an action outside the agent itself.
google_dialogflow_transition_route_group: `google_dialogflow_transition_route_group` is a reusable set of transition rules shared across multiple pages in a Dialogflow CX flow, avoiding duplicating the same routing logic on every page.
google_dialogflow_version: `google_dialogflow_version` is an immutable, named snapshot of a Dialogflow agent's own configuration at a point in time, deployable to an environment independently of ongoing draft changes.
google_dialogflow_webhook: `google_dialogflow_webhook` configures an external HTTP endpoint a Dialogflow agent calls during a conversation to run custom business logic or fetch dynamic data.
google_discoveryengine_assistant: `google_discoveryengine_assistant` configures a conversational assistant experience (grounded answers, follow-up suggestions) built on top of a Discovery Engine (recently rebranded Agent Search) data store or engine.
google_discoveryengine_control: `google_discoveryengine_control` defines a rule that adjusts search or recommendation behavior for matching queries, e.g. boosting, burying, or redirecting results for a specific search term.
google_discoveryengine_conversation: `google_discoveryengine_conversation` is a single multi-turn conversation session against a Discovery Engine search app, holding the exchanged query/reply pairs so follow-up questions retain context.
google_discoveryengine_data_store: `google_discoveryengine_data_store` is the indexed content repository (structured, unstructured, or website data) that a Discovery Engine search or recommendation app is built on top of.
google_discoveryengine_document: `google_discoveryengine_document` is a single indexed item (a webpage, a structured record, a file) within a Discovery Engine data store, the unit search and recommendation results are returned as.
google_discoveryengine_engine: `google_discoveryengine_engine` is the deployable search, recommendation, or chat application built on top of one or more Discovery Engine data stores, the resource a serving config is created under.
google_discoveryengine_identity_mapping_: `google_discoveryengine_identity_mapping_store` holds the mapping between a caller's own external user identities and the access-control principal used to filter Discovery Engine search results to only the documents that user is permitted to see.
google_discoveryengine_license_config: `google_discoveryengine_license_config` defines a named license tier used to track and assign per-user Discovery Engine / Agent Search entitlements within an organization.
google_discoveryengine_push_notification: `google_discoveryengine_push_notification_config` configures an endpoint Discovery Engine sends push notification(s) to when a relevant event (e.g. a new matching document) occurs.
google_discoveryengine_schema: `google_discoveryengine_schema` defines the field structure (names, types) that structured documents in a Discovery Engine data store must conform to.
google_discoveryengine_serving_config: `google_discoveryengine_serving_config` defines the tunable ranking and business-logic configuration (boosting, filtering, model selection) applied when a Discovery Engine app actually serves search or recommendation results.
google_discoveryengine_session: `google_discoveryengine_session` is a stateful session tracking a user's own sequence of interactions with a Discovery Engine app, used to personalize recommendations or maintain conversational context.
google_discoveryengine_target_site: `google_discoveryengine_target_site` registers a specific website (or a URL pattern within one) to be crawled and indexed into a Discovery Engine data store's own website search content.
google_dlp_connection: `google_dlp_connection` registers credentials Sensitive Data Protection uses to connect to and scan an external or non-native data source (e.g. a JDBC database) for sensitive data discovery.
google_dlp_content_policy: `google_dlp_content_policy` defines organization-wide default configuration (inspection templates, discovery settings) automatically applied across Sensitive Data Protection scans unless a scan overrides it.
google_dlp_deidentify_template: `google_dlp_deidentify_template` is a reusable, saved configuration of de-identification transformations (masking, tokenization, redaction) Sensitive Data Protection applies when scrubbing sensitive data from content.
google_dlp_discovery_config: `google_dlp_discovery_config` configures Sensitive Data Protection to automatically and continuously scan data assets across an org, project, or specific resource for sensitive data, rather than requiring a manually triggered job.
google_dlp_dlp_job: `google_dlp_dlp_job` is a single execution of a Sensitive Data Protection inspection or risk-analysis scan against a specified data source.
google_dlp_inspect_template: `google_dlp_inspect_template` is a reusable, saved configuration of which info type(s) and rule(s) Sensitive Data Protection looks for when scanning content.
google_dlp_job_trigger: `google_dlp_job_trigger` schedules a Sensitive Data Protection inspection job to run automatically on a recurring basis against a defined data source.
google_dlp_stored_info_type: `google_dlp_stored_info_type` defines a custom, reusable sensitive-data pattern (a dictionary or regex) Sensitive Data Protection scans can detect, beyond its own built-in info types.
google_dns_change: `google_dns_change` is a single atomic batch of record additions and deletions applied to a Cloud DNS managed zone.
google_dns_managed_zone: `google_dns_managed_zone` is a Cloud DNS zone -- a container of DNS record(s) for a specific domain, either publicly resolvable or private to a set of VPC networks.
google_dns_policy: `google_dns_policy` configures DNS behavior (custom forwarding targets, DNS logging) applied to VPC network(s) attached to it, for private and split-horizon DNS scenarios.
google_dns_resource_record_set: `google_dns_resource_record_set` is a single DNS record set (e.g. an `A` or `MX` record) within a Cloud DNS managed zone.
google_dns_response_policy: `google_dns_response_policy` overrides standard DNS resolution for VPC network(s) it's attached to, letting queries for specific names return caller-defined responses instead of the real internet answer.
google_dns_response_policy_rule: `google_dns_response_policy_rule` defines the override response for a specific hostname or wildcard pattern within a Cloud DNS response policy.
google_eventarc_channel: `google_eventarc_channel` is the ingestion point third-party event provider(s) publish CloudEvents-formatted event(s) into, so Eventarc triggers can route them onward.
google_eventarc_channel_connection: `google_eventarc_channel_connection` links an Eventarc channel to a specific third-party event provider's own registered connection, authorizing that provider to publish events into the channel.
google_eventarc_enrollment: `google_eventarc_enrollment` subscribes a specific pipeline or destination to receive matching event(s) flowing through an Eventarc message bus.
google_eventarc_google_api_source: `google_eventarc_google_api_source` configures Eventarc to receive Google Cloud audit log-derived events for a defined set of Google API method(s), publishing them onto a message bus.
google_eventarc_message_buse: `google_eventarc_message_buse` (a Message Bus) is Eventarc's central event routing hub that publishers send event(s) into and enrollment(s) subscribe destination(s) to receive matching event(s) from, the newer alternative to point-to-point triggers.
google_eventarc_pipeline: `google_eventarc_pipeline` transforms and forwards event(s) flowing through Eventarc from a message bus to one or more destination(s), optionally applying a transformation template along the way.
google_eventarc_trigger: `google_eventarc_trigger` routes matching event(s) (from a Google Cloud service, a custom channel, or a third-party source) directly to a single destination such as Cloud Run, the original point-to-point Eventarc routing model.
google_firebaseapphosting_backend: `google_firebaseapphosting_backend` is a Firebase App Hosting backend, the deployable web app resource that build(s) and rollout(s) are created for.
google_firebaseapphosting_build: `google_firebaseapphosting_build` is a single compiled build of a Firebase App Hosting backend's own source code, produced from a Git push and deployable via a rollout.
google_firebaseapphosting_domain: `google_firebaseapphosting_domain` maps a custom domain to a Firebase App Hosting backend.
google_firebaseapphosting_rollout: `google_firebaseapphosting_rollout` deploys a specific build to live traffic on a Firebase App Hosting backend.
google_firestore_backup_schedule: `google_firestore_backup_schedule` automates recurring Firestore database backups on a defined cadence, instead of requiring each backup to be triggered manually.
google_firestore_change_stream: `google_firestore_change_stream` continuously streams a Firestore database's own document changes (creates, updates, deletes) for a collection group or the whole database, for change-data-capture style integrations.
google_firestore_database: `google_firestore_database` is a Firestore database, the top-level document/collection data store within a Google Cloud project -- a project can have multiple Firestore databases.
google_firestore_index: `google_firestore_index` defines a composite or single-field index on a Firestore database, required for certain query shapes (e.g. filtering and sorting on different fields) to run efficiently.
google_firestore_user_cred: `google_firestore_user_cred` is a database-scoped credential Firestore issues for authenticating directly to a specific database, independent of and narrower in scope than a Google Cloud IAM principal.
google_gkebackup_backup: `google_gkebackup_backup` is a point-in-time backup of a GKE cluster's own workload configuration and (optionally) persistent volume data, created from a backup plan.
google_gkebackup_backup_channel: `google_gkebackup_backup_channel` establishes cross-project connectivity letting a GKE backup plan back up a cluster running in a different project than the backup itself is stored in.
google_gkebackup_backup_plan: `google_gkebackup_backup_plan` defines what a GKE Backup for GKE backup covers (which namespaces/resources) and how often it runs automatically.
google_gkebackup_restore: `google_gkebackup_restore` restores a GKE backup's own workload configuration and data into a target cluster, executed according to a restore plan.
google_gkebackup_restore_channel: `google_gkebackup_restore_channel` establishes cross-project connectivity letting a GKE restore plan restore a backup into a cluster running in a different project than the backup itself.
google_gkebackup_restore_plan: `google_gkebackup_restore_plan` defines how a GKE backup is restored -- which target cluster and what conflict-resolution/transformation rules apply -- when a restore is executed.
google_gkeonprem_bare_metal_admin_cluste: `google_gkeonprem_bare_metal_admin_cluster` is the administrative GKE on Bare Metal cluster that manages the lifecycle of other bare metal user cluster(s) running on the same on-premises hardware.
google_gkeonprem_bare_metal_cluster: `google_gkeonprem_bare_metal_cluster` is a GKE on Bare Metal user cluster, running Kubernetes workloads directly on caller-provided physical or virtual machines rather than Google Cloud VMs.
google_gkeonprem_bare_metal_node_pool: `google_gkeonprem_bare_metal_node_pool` is a group of worker node(s) with shared configuration within a GKE on Bare Metal cluster.
google_gkeonprem_vmware_admin_cluster: `google_gkeonprem_vmware_admin_cluster` is the administrative GKE on VMware cluster that manages the lifecycle of other VMware user cluster(s) running on the same vSphere environment.
google_gkeonprem_vmware_cluster: `google_gkeonprem_vmware_cluster` is a GKE on VMware user cluster, running Kubernetes workloads on VMware vSphere infrastructure rather than Google Cloud VMs.
google_gkeonprem_vmware_node_pool: `google_gkeonprem_vmware_node_pool` is a group of worker node(s) with shared configuration within a GKE on VMware cluster.
google_healthcare_attribute_definition: `google_healthcare_attribute_definition` defines a named consent attribute (e.g. a patient's own opt-in category) that consent artifacts in a Cloud Healthcare API consent store can be evaluated against.
google_healthcare_consent: `google_healthcare_consent` records a single patient's own consent decision (granted or revoked) for a defined use of their health data, managed within a Cloud Healthcare API consent store.
google_healthcare_consent_artifact: `google_healthcare_consent_artifact` is the immutable record of evidence (e.g. a signed consent form) supporting a specific consent decision in a Cloud Healthcare API consent store.
google_healthcare_consent_store: `google_healthcare_consent_store` holds patient consent record(s) and their own supporting artifact(s), letting Cloud Healthcare API data access be automatically checked against recorded patient consent.
google_healthcare_dataset: `google_healthcare_dataset` is the top-level container in the Cloud Healthcare API that FHIR, DICOM, and HL7v2 store(s) are created within, grouping related health data under shared location and access policy.
google_healthcare_dicom_store: `google_healthcare_dicom_store` is a managed store for DICOM medical imaging data within the Cloud Healthcare API, exposing a DICOMweb-compatible interface for image storage and retrieval.
google_healthcare_fhir_store: `google_healthcare_fhir_store` is a managed store for FHIR-formatted clinical data within the Cloud Healthcare API, exposing a standards-compliant FHIR REST interface.
google_healthcare_hl7_v2_store: `google_healthcare_hl7_v2_store` is a managed store for HL7v2 messages within the Cloud Healthcare API, used for ingesting and routing clinical messaging traffic from legacy healthcare systems.
google_healthcare_message: `google_healthcare_message` is a single ingested HL7v2 message stored within a Cloud Healthcare API HL7v2 store.
google_healthcare_user_data_mapping: `google_healthcare_user_data_mapping` links a specific piece of health data to the patient user it belongs to, within a Cloud Healthcare API consent store, so consent decisions can be evaluated per patient.
google_logging_bucket: `google_logging_bucket` is a Cloud Logging log bucket, the storage container ingested log entries are retained in for a configured retention period and made queryable from.
google_logging_exclusion: `google_logging_exclusion` filters out matching log entries before they're ingested into a Cloud Logging sink or bucket, reducing storage cost and noise for logs that don't need to be kept.
google_logging_link: `google_logging_link` links a Cloud Logging log bucket to a BigQuery dataset, enabling that bucket's own log data to be queried directly with SQL via BigQuery's own analytics engine.
google_logging_log_scope: `google_logging_log_scope` defines a named set of log bucket(s) or resource(s) that a Cloud Logging query can be scoped to search across together.
google_logging_metric: `google_logging_metric` defines a user-created metric derived from matching Cloud Logging log entries (e.g. a count of error-level logs), queryable and alertable through Cloud Monitoring.
google_logging_saved_query: `google_logging_saved_query` is a named, reusable Cloud Logging query saved for repeated use in the Logs Explorer, instead of re-entering the same filter each time.
google_logging_sink: `google_logging_sink` routes matching Cloud Logging log entries to an external destination (a Cloud Storage bucket, BigQuery dataset, or Pub/Sub topic) for export outside the default logging retention.
google_logging_view: `google_logging_view` restricts a principal's own access within a Cloud Logging log bucket to a defined filtered subset of its log entries, for role-based data isolation.
google_managedkafka_acl: `google_managedkafka_acl` defines a Kafka access control list entry restricting which principal(s) may perform a given operation (read, write, and similar) against a resource in a Managed Service for Apache Kafka cluster.
google_managedkafka_cluster: `google_managedkafka_cluster` provisions a fully managed Apache Kafka cluster through Google Cloud's own Managed Service for Apache Kafka.
google_managedkafka_connect_cluster: `google_managedkafka_connect_cluster` provisions a managed Kafka Connect cluster, the runtime connector(s) execute on to move data between a Managed Kafka cluster and external systems.
google_managedkafka_connector: `google_managedkafka_connector` configures a single Kafka Connect source or sink connector running on a Managed Kafka Connect cluster, moving data between Kafka and an external system.
google_managedkafka_schema_registry: `google_managedkafka_schema_registry` is a managed Kafka schema registry, storing and versioning the message schema(s) producers and consumers on a Managed Kafka cluster validate against.
google_managedkafka_topic: `google_managedkafka_topic` is a Kafka topic within a Managed Service for Apache Kafka cluster, the named stream producers publish to and consumers read from.
google_managedkafka_version: `google_managedkafka_version` reports a specific schema version registered within a Managed Kafka schema registry subject.
google_migrationcenter_assets_export_job: `google_migrationcenter_assets_export_job` exports discovered asset inventory data from Migration Center to an external destination (e.g. BigQuery), for reporting or integration outside the console.
google_migrationcenter_discovery_client: `google_migrationcenter_discovery_client` registers a Migration Center discovery agent instance deployed in a source environment, that scans and reports on-premises or other-cloud asset(s) back to Migration Center.
google_migrationcenter_group: `google_migrationcenter_group` is a named collection of discovered asset(s) within Migration Center, used to scope a sizing report or migration wave to a specific subset of infrastructure.
google_migrationcenter_import_data_file: `google_migrationcenter_import_data_file` is a single uploaded file (e.g. an exported CSV inventory) processed as part of a Migration Center bulk asset import job.
google_migrationcenter_import_job: `google_migrationcenter_import_job` runs a bulk import of asset inventory data into Migration Center from uploaded file(s), rather than live discovery agent scanning.
google_migrationcenter_preference_set: `google_migrationcenter_preference_set` defines the sizing preferences (target region, machine series, commitment terms) Migration Center applies when generating a migration recommendation and cost estimate for a set of assets.
google_migrationcenter_report: `google_migrationcenter_report` is a generated Migration Center sizing and cost report for a specific group of assets under a chosen preference set, recommending target Google Cloud resources.
google_migrationcenter_report_config: `google_migrationcenter_report_config` defines the reusable configuration (which asset group and preference set to use) a Migration Center report is generated from.
google_migrationcenter_source: `google_migrationcenter_source` registers the origin (a discovery client, an import job, or a manually entered environment) that Migration Center asset data was collected from.
google_ml_job: `google_ml_job` runs a training or batch prediction job on the legacy AI Platform (ML Engine) service, the predecessor to Vertex AI's own custom training and batch prediction.
google_ml_model: `google_ml_model` is a container for a trained model's own version(s) on the legacy AI Platform (ML Engine) service.
google_ml_study: `google_ml_study` is the top-level configuration for a legacy AI Platform hyperparameter tuning study, defining the parameter search space and objective its trial(s) are evaluated against.
google_ml_trial: `google_ml_trial` is a single parameter combination evaluated as part of a legacy AI Platform hyperparameter tuning study.
google_ml_version: `google_ml_version` is a specific, deployable version of a model on the legacy AI Platform (ML Engine) service, servable for online prediction.
google_monitoring_alert_policy: `google_monitoring_alert_policy` defines the condition(s) Cloud Monitoring evaluates against incoming metric, log, or uptime data, firing an alert and notifying configured channel(s) when they're met.
google_monitoring_group: `google_monitoring_group` is a saved, dynamic grouping of monitored resources (e.g. all VMs matching a name pattern) that Cloud Monitoring dashboards and alerts can be scoped to.
google_monitoring_metric_descriptor: `google_monitoring_metric_descriptor` defines a custom metric type -- its own name, value type, and labels -- that application-written data points can be reported against in Cloud Monitoring.
google_monitoring_notification_channel: `google_monitoring_notification_channel` configures a destination (email, Slack, PagerDuty, webhook, and similar) Cloud Monitoring alert policies send notifications to when they fire.
google_monitoring_service: `google_monitoring_service` represents a logical service (e.g. one microservice or app) within Cloud Monitoring, the entity a service level objective is defined and measured against.
google_monitoring_service_level_objectiv: `google_monitoring_service_level_objective` defines a target reliability goal (e.g. 99.9% availability over 30 days) for a Cloud Monitoring service, tracked against a chosen service level indicator.
google_monitoring_snooz: `google_monitoring_snooz` (a Snooze) temporarily suppresses notifications from matching Cloud Monitoring alert policies for a defined time window, e.g. during planned maintenance.
google_monitoring_uptime_check_config: `google_monitoring_uptime_check_config` configures Cloud Monitoring to periodically probe an HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP endpoint from multiple global locations, reporting the results as uptime and latency data.
google_netapp_active_directory: `google_netapp_active_directory` registers an Active Directory domain connection Google Cloud NetApp Volumes uses to authenticate SMB and Kerberized NFS access to its own volumes.
google_netapp_backup: `google_netapp_backup` is a single point-in-time backup of a Google Cloud NetApp Volumes volume, stored independently of the volume's own snapshot history for longer-term retention.
google_netapp_backup_policy: `google_netapp_backup_policy` defines the automated backup schedule (frequency, retention) applied to Google Cloud NetApp Volumes volume(s) it's attached to.
google_netapp_backup_vault: `google_netapp_backup_vault` is the storage container Google Cloud NetApp Volumes backups are written into and organized under.
google_netapp_host_group: `google_netapp_host_group` defines a named group of client host IP address(es) Google Cloud NetApp Volumes export policy rules can reference together.
google_netapp_kms_config: `google_netapp_kms_config` configures the Cloud KMS customer-managed encryption key Google Cloud NetApp Volumes uses to encrypt a storage pool's own volume(s).
google_netapp_quota_rule: `google_netapp_quota_rule` sets a per-user or per-group storage quota on a Google Cloud NetApp Volumes volume, limiting how much space or how many files that user or group may consume.
google_netapp_replication: `google_netapp_replication` configures cross-region or cross-zone replication of a Google Cloud NetApp Volumes volume to a destination volume, for disaster recovery.
google_netapp_snapshot: `google_netapp_snapshot` is a point-in-time, storage-efficient snapshot of a Google Cloud NetApp Volumes volume, restorable in place or usable as the source for a new volume clone.
google_netapp_storage_pool: `google_netapp_storage_pool` is the underlying provisioned capacity and performance tier in Google Cloud NetApp Volumes that individual volume(s) are carved out of.
google_netapp_volume: `google_netapp_volume` is a managed NFS or SMB file share provisioned from a Google Cloud NetApp Volumes storage pool, mountable by Compute Engine VMs, GKE, or other clients.
google_networkconnectivity_automated_dns: `google_networkconnectivity_automated_dns_record` is a DNS record Network Connectivity Center automatically creates and manages for a Private Service Connect connection, resolving a service's own domain name to the connection's private address.
google_networkconnectivity_destination: `google_networkconnectivity_destination` defines a routable target (e.g. a set of IP prefixes) that Network Connectivity Center's policy-based routing rules can direct traffic toward.
google_networkconnectivity_gateway_adver: `google_networkconnectivity_gateway_advertised_route` is a route a Network Connectivity Center gateway advertises out to its own connected spoke(s), controlling what destinations the hub tells other spokes are reachable.
google_networkconnectivity_hub: `google_networkconnectivity_hub` is the central resource in Network Connectivity Center that VPC network(s), VPN/interconnect connections, and other spoke(s) attach to, enabling any-to-any connectivity across them.
google_networkconnectivity_internal_rang: `google_networkconnectivity_internal_range` reserves a named block of internal IP address space for a VPC network ahead of time, so subnet allocation can draw from a pre-planned, non-overlapping pool.
google_networkconnectivity_multicloud_da: `google_networkconnectivity_multicloud_data_transfer_config` configures Data Transfer Essentials billing for data transferred from Google Cloud to another cloud provider over Cross-Cloud Interconnect, defining the eligible destination(s) discounted pricing applies to.
google_networkconnectivity_policy_based_: `google_networkconnectivity_policy_based_route` overrides a VPC network's own default destination-based routing with a rule matched on additional criteria (e.g. source IP or protocol), for traffic-steering scenarios standard routes can't express.
google_networkconnectivity_psc_authoriza: `google_networkconnectivity_psc_authorization_policy` restricts which consumer project(s) or network(s) are permitted to establish a Private Service Connect connection to a service published behind a Network Connectivity Center hub.
google_networkconnectivity_regional_endp: `google_networkconnectivity_regional_endpoint` creates a regional Private Service Connect endpoint for reaching a Google API or a published service, an alternative to a zonal or global endpoint for regionally-scoped connectivity.
google_networkconnectivity_service_conne: `google_networkconnectivity_service_connection_map` defines which producer service(s) a consumer network is permitted to connect to via Private Service Connect automation, and which subnet(s) those connections draw addresses from.

`google_networkconnectivity_service_connection_policy` configures the automated Private Service Connect connection settings (subnet allocation, PSC connection limits) applied when a consumer network connects to a specific managed service.

`google_networkconnectivity_service_connection_token` is a one-time credential a service producer issues to authorize a specific consumer network to establish a Private Service Connect connection to its own service.
google_networkconnectivity_spoke: `google_networkconnectivity_spoke` attaches a single network resource (a VPC network, VPN tunnel, interconnect attachment, or router appliance) to a Network Connectivity Center hub, making it part of that hub's own any-to-any topology.
google_networkconnectivity_transport: `google_networkconnectivity_transport` defines the underlying transport-layer resource (e.g. a specific interconnect or VPN tunnel) a Network Connectivity Center spoke's own connectivity is actually carried over.
google_networksecurity_address_group: `google_networksecurity_address_group` is a named, reusable list of IP address(es) or CIDR range(s) that Cloud Firewall or Cloud Armor policy rules can reference by name instead of enumerating addresses inline.
google_networksecurity_authorization_pol: `google_networksecurity_authorization_policy` defines an allow/deny access-control rule for traffic reaching a load balancer or service mesh backend, evaluated based on the caller's own authenticated identity.
google_networksecurity_authz_policy: `google_networksecurity_authz_policy` (AuthzPolicy) is the current-generation authorization policy resource for Cloud Service Mesh and external Application Load Balancers, controlling which authenticated caller(s) may reach a given gateway or backend.
google_networksecurity_backend_authentic: `google_networksecurity_backend_authentication_config` configures a load balancer to authenticate itself to backend services via mutual TLS, referencing the client certificate presented on outbound connections.
google_networksecurity_client_tls_policy: `google_networksecurity_client_tls_policy` configures the TLS settings (client certificate, trusted server CA) a Google Cloud service uses when it acts as the TLS client connecting outbound to another service.
google_networksecurity_dns_threat_detect: `google_networksecurity_dns_threat_detector` enables DNS Armor, which sends a project's own internet-bound DNS query logs to a managed Infoblox threat-detection engine to flag malicious domains in real time.
google_networksecurity_firewall_endpoint: `google_networksecurity_firewall_endpoint` is a zonal, Google-managed data-plane resource that Cloud NGFW's own intrusion prevention service uses to transparently inspect workload traffic against threat signatures.
`google_networksecurity_firewall_endpoint_association` attaches a VPC network to a firewall endpoint, enabling Cloud NGFW intrusion prevention inspection for that network's own traffic.
google_networksecurity_gateway_security_: `google_networksecurity_gateway_security_policy` defines a URL and content-filtering policy applied by a Secure Web Proxy gateway to outbound web traffic.
google_networksecurity_intercept_deploym: `google_networksecurity_intercept_deployment` is a zonal instance of a third-party network security appliance deployed under Google Cloud's Network Security Integration framework, that intercepted traffic is forwarded to for inspection.
`google_networksecurity_intercept_deployment_group` groups related intercept deployments together across zones, forwarding traffic to the appropriate zonal deployment based on its own source.
google_networksecurity_intercept_endpoin: `google_networksecurity_intercept_endpoint_group` is the traffic-interception entry point associated with an intercept deployment group, that VPC network traffic is routed through for third-party security appliance inspection.
`google_networksecurity_intercept_endpoint_group_association` attaches a VPC network to an intercept endpoint group, enabling Network Security Integration traffic interception for that network.
google_networksecurity_mirroring_deploym: `google_networksecurity_mirroring_deployment` is a zonal instance of a third-party security or monitoring appliance under Google Cloud's Network Security Integration framework, that mirrored packet copies are sent to for out-of-band analysis.

`google_networksecurity_mirroring_deployment_group` groups related packet-mirroring deployments together across zones, forwarding mirrored traffic to the appropriate zonal deployment based on its own source.
google_networksecurity_mirroring_endpoin: `google_networksecurity_mirroring_endpoint_group` is the packet-mirroring entry point associated with a mirroring deployment group, that VPC network traffic copies are routed through.

`google_networksecurity_mirroring_endpoint_group_association` attaches a VPC network to a mirroring endpoint group, enabling packet mirroring under Network Security Integration for that network's own traffic.
google_networksecurity_rule: `google_networksecurity_rule` is a single match-and-action rule within a Cloud NGFW gateway security policy or address group, evaluated against matching traffic.
google_networksecurity_sac_attachment: `google_networksecurity_sac_attachment` is a regional Secure Access Connect resource that enables an NCC Gateway to process traffic through a connected security service edge (SSE) provider, e.g. Palo Alto Prisma Access.
google_networksecurity_sac_realm: `google_networksecurity_sac_realm` is the global Secure Access Connect resource linking a Google Cloud project to a security service edge (SSE) provider, the parent resource its own regional attachments are created under.
google_networksecurity_security_profile: `google_networksecurity_security_profile` defines the inspection behavior (threat prevention settings, custom signatures) applied by a Cloud NGFW intrusion prevention or Secure Web Proxy security profile group.
google_networksecurity_security_profile_: `google_networksecurity_security_profile_group` bundles one or more security profiles together for reference from a single firewall policy rule.
google_networksecurity_server_tls_policy: `google_networksecurity_server_tls_policy` configures the TLS settings (server certificate, client validation mode) a Google Cloud service uses when it acts as the TLS server terminating inbound connections.
google_networksecurity_tls_inspection_po: `google_networksecurity_tls_inspection_policy` configures Cloud NGFW to decrypt, inspect, and re-encrypt TLS traffic passing through a firewall policy, using a Certificate Authority Service CA pool to mint the inspection certificates.
google_networksecurity_url_list: `google_networksecurity_url_list` is a named, reusable list of URL pattern(s) that a Secure Web Proxy or Cloud NGFW policy rule can reference by name instead of enumerating URLs inline.
google_networkservices_agent_connectivit: `google_networkservices_agent_connectivity_template` defines a reusable connectivity configuration (ingress/egress mode, policy defaults) that Agent Gateway deployments on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform are created from.
google_networkservices_agent_gateway: `google_networkservices_agent_gateway` deploys Agent Gateway, the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform's own networking component that secures and governs traffic between users and agents, agents and tools, or agents and other agents.
google_networkservices_authz_extension: `google_networkservices_authz_extension` calls out to an external authorization service as part of a Cloud Service Mesh or load balancer request path, letting a custom service decide whether to allow or deny each request.
google_networkservices_endpoint_policy: `google_networkservices_endpoint_policy` configures the traffic behavior (mTLS, logging) a proxyless gRPC or sidecar-based workload applies to inbound connections in a Cloud Service Mesh.
google_networkservices_extension_binding: `google_networkservices_extension_binding` attaches a Service Extension (a WASM plugin or external callout) to a specific load balancer or gateway resource, activating it for that resource's own traffic.
google_networkservices_gateway: `google_networkservices_gateway` is the Traffic Director/Cloud Service Mesh resource defining a data-plane listener (address, port, routing type) that traffic enters through before being matched to a route.
google_networkservices_grpc_route: `google_networkservices_grpc_route` defines routing rule(s) for gRPC traffic within a Cloud Service Mesh, matching on service/method and directing matching requests to a specific backend.
google_networkservices_http_route: `google_networkservices_http_route` defines routing rule(s) for HTTP traffic within a Cloud Service Mesh or through a gateway, matching on path/header/method and directing matching requests to a specific backend.
google_networkservices_lb_edge_extension: `google_networkservices_lb_edge_extension` runs a Service Extension at a load balancer's own edge, letting it influence backend selection and Cloud CDN cache key computation by modifying request headers before caching/routing decisions are made.
google_networkservices_lb_route_extensio: `google_networkservices_lb_route_extension` runs a Service Extension after routing decisions are made on a load balancer, letting it modify the request or response as part of the route match.
google_networkservices_lb_traffic_extens: `google_networkservices_lb_traffic_extension` runs a Service Extension against a load balancer's own traffic before routing, letting external logic inspect or modify requests and responses passing through.
google_networkservices_mesh: `google_networkservices_mesh` is the top-level Cloud Service Mesh resource that gRPC and HTTP route(s) are attached to, defining the logical service mesh workloads participate in.
google_networkservices_multicast_consume: `google_networkservices_multicast_consumer_association` grants a specific VPC network permission to consume (receive) traffic from a Cloud Multicast group range, part of Google Cloud's own real IP multicast support for VPC.
google_networkservices_multicast_group_c: `google_networkservices_multicast_group_consumer_activation` activates a previously associated consumer VPC network to actually start receiving traffic from a specific Cloud Multicast group.
google_networkservices_producer_extensio: `google_networkservices_producer_extension` runs a Service Extension on the producer side of a Private Service Connect-published service, letting the producer inspect or modify traffic before it reaches the underlying service.
google_networkservices_service_binding: `google_networkservices_service_binding` links a Cloud Service Mesh route to a Service Directory service entry, resolving mesh traffic to endpoints registered outside Google Cloud's own native compute.
google_networkservices_service_lb_policy: `google_networkservices_service_lb_policy` configures load-balancing behavior (e.g. auto-capacity draining, isolation) applied across the backend(s) of a Cloud Service Mesh or load-balanced backend service.
google_networkservices_tcp_route: `google_networkservices_tcp_route` defines routing rule(s) for raw TCP traffic within a Cloud Service Mesh, matching on port and directing matching connections to a specific backend.
google_networkservices_tls_route: `google_networkservices_tls_route` defines routing rule(s) for TLS traffic within a Cloud Service Mesh, matching on SNI and directing matching connections to a specific backend without terminating TLS.
google_networkservices_version: `google_networkservices_version` is a specific, addressable revision of a Network Services resource used to reference a fixed configuration rather than always the latest.
google_networkservices_wasm_plugin: `google_networkservices_wasm_plugin` deploys a caller-authored WebAssembly module as a Service Extension, running custom request/response processing logic inline on a load balancer or service mesh's own data path.
google_oracledatabase_autonomous_databas: `google_oracledatabase_autonomous_database` provisions a self-managing Oracle Autonomous Database instance through Oracle Database@Google Cloud, running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure but integrated into a Google Cloud project.
google_oracledatabase_cloud_exadata_infr: `google_oracledatabase_cloud_exadata_infrastructure` provisions the dedicated Exadata hardware infrastructure that Oracle Database@Google Cloud VM cluster(s) are created on.
google_oracledatabase_cloud_vm_cluster: `google_oracledatabase_cloud_vm_cluster` provisions a cluster of VM(s) on Oracle Exadata infrastructure within Oracle Database@Google Cloud, that Oracle database instance(s) run on.
google_oracledatabase_db_system: `google_oracledatabase_db_system` provisions an Oracle Base Database Service system through Oracle Database@Google Cloud, a lighter-weight (non-Exadata) managed Oracle database deployment.
google_oracledatabase_exadb_vm_cluster: `google_oracledatabase_exadb_vm_cluster` provisions an Exadata VM cluster on Exascale Infrastructure through Oracle Database@Google Cloud, backed by an Exascale storage vault rather than fixed, pre-allocated Exadata storage.
google_oracledatabase_exascale_db_storag: `google_oracledatabase_exascale_db_storage_vault` provisions a shared, instantly and non-disruptively expandable storage pool that one or more Exadata VM clusters on Exascale Infrastructure draw their own database storage from.
google_oracledatabase_goldengate_connect: `google_oracledatabase_goldengate_connection` defines a connection GoldenGate uses to reach a source or target database for real-time data replication, as part of Oracle Database@Google Cloud.

`google_oracledatabase_goldengate_connection_assignment` assigns a GoldenGate connection to a specific GoldenGate deployment, making that source or target database available to that deployment's own replication task(s).
google_oracledatabase_goldengate_deploym: `google_oracledatabase_goldengate_deployment` provisions a managed Oracle GoldenGate instance through Oracle Database@Google Cloud, used for real-time data replication and integration between databases.
google_oracledatabase_odb_network: `google_oracledatabase_odb_network` provisions the dedicated network Oracle Database@Google Cloud infrastructure (Exadata, Exascale VM clusters) is deployed into, peered with a Google Cloud VPC network for connectivity.
google_oracledatabase_odb_subnet: `google_oracledatabase_odb_subnet` defines a subnet within an Oracle Database@Google Cloud ODB network, the IP address range Exadata or Exascale VM cluster resources are allocated from.
google_privateca_ca_pool: `google_privateca_ca_pool` groups related Certificate Authority Service certificate authorities together, sharing issuance policy and letting certificates be requested from the pool without pinning to one specific CA.
google_privateca_certificate: `google_privateca_certificate` is an X.509 certificate issued by a Certificate Authority Service CA, either directly requested or generated from a Certificate Manager Google-managed certificate.
google_privateca_certificate_authority: `google_privateca_certificate_authority` is a private Certificate Authority managed by Certificate Authority Service, issuing X.509 certificate(s) within its own CA pool.
google_privateca_certificate_template: `google_privateca_certificate_template` constrains and pre-fills the fields a Certificate Authority Service CA is permitted to issue certificates with, enforcing organizational certificate policy.
google_pubsub_schema: `google_pubsub_schema` defines the Avro or Protocol Buffer message schema a Pub/Sub topic's own published messages are validated against.
google_pubsub_snapshot: `google_pubsub_snapshot` captures a Pub/Sub subscription's own acknowledgment state at a point in time, letting the subscription be seeked back to it later to replay messages.
google_pubsub_subscription: `google_pubsub_subscription` attaches to a Pub/Sub topic and delivers its own published messages to a consumer, either by pull or push, tracking per-message acknowledgment.
google_pubsub_topic: `google_pubsub_topic` is a Pub/Sub topic, the named resource publishers send message(s) to and subscription(s) receive message(s) from.
google_run_instance: `google_run_instance` is a single running container instance backing a Cloud Run service or job, the unit that actually executes request or task handling.
google_run_job: `google_run_job` runs a Cloud Run container to completion for a batch or scheduled task, rather than serving ongoing request traffic like a Cloud Run service.
google_run_service: `google_run_service` is a Cloud Run service, a deployed, autoscaling container that serves HTTP request traffic.
google_run_worker_pool: `google_run_worker_pool` runs a Cloud Run container that continuously processes work (e.g. from a queue) rather than serving inbound HTTP requests or running to completion like a job.
google_securesourcemanager_branch_rule: `google_securesourcemanager_branch_rule` enforces protections (required reviews, status checks, restricted force-push) on branch(es) matching a pattern within a Secure Source Manager repository.
google_securesourcemanager_hook: `google_securesourcemanager_hook` configures a webhook that Secure Source Manager calls out to on repository events (pushes, pull request changes), integrating with external CI/CD or notification systems.
google_securesourcemanager_instance: `google_securesourcemanager_instance` is the top-level, privately hosted Secure Source Manager deployment that repository/repositories are created within, isolated to a single Google Cloud project and VPC.
google_securesourcemanager_issue: `google_securesourcemanager_issue` is a tracked issue within a Secure Source Manager repository, used for bug and task tracking alongside the source code itself.
google_securesourcemanager_issue_comment: `google_securesourcemanager_issue_comment` is a single comment posted on a Secure Source Manager issue.
google_securesourcemanager_pull_request: `google_securesourcemanager_pull_request` proposes merging one branch into another within a Secure Source Manager repository, the unit code review and CI checks are attached to before merge.
google_securesourcemanager_pull_request_: `google_securesourcemanager_pull_request_comment` is a single review comment posted on a Secure Source Manager pull request, either general or attached to a specific line of the diff.
google_securesourcemanager_repository: `google_securesourcemanager_repository` is a Git repository hosted within a Secure Source Manager instance, Google Cloud's own fully managed, private source code hosting service.
google_securitycenter_big_query_export: `google_securitycenter_big_query_export` continuously streams Security Command Center finding(s) into a BigQuery dataset for custom analysis, dashboards, or long-term retention.
google_securitycenter_custom_module: `google_securitycenter_custom_module` defines a caller-written detection rule Security Command Center's Security Health Analytics evaluates alongside its own built-in detectors.
google_securitycenter_mute_config: `google_securitycenter_mute_config` automatically mutes matching Security Command Center finding(s), suppressing them from active alerting while keeping them recorded.
google_securitycenter_notification_confi: `google_securitycenter_notification_config` streams matching Security Command Center finding(s) to a Pub/Sub topic in real time as they're created or updated.
google_securitycenter_source: `google_securitycenter_source` registers an external or custom detector as a finding source within Security Command Center, letting it publish its own finding(s) alongside Google's built-in detectors.
google_spanner_backup: `google_spanner_backup` is a point-in-time backup of a Spanner database, restorable to a new database within the same instance.
google_spanner_backup_schedule: `google_spanner_backup_schedule` automates recurring Spanner database backups on a defined cadence, instead of requiring each backup to be triggered manually.
google_spanner_database: `google_spanner_database` is a Spanner database, the schema and data container created within a Spanner instance that queries and transactions run against.
google_spanner_instance: `google_spanner_instance` is the top-level Spanner resource that provisions compute capacity (nodes or processing units) database(s) run on, and defines the region(s) data is replicated across.
google_spanner_instance_config: `google_spanner_instance_config` defines the geographic replication topology (which region(s) hold a read-write or read-only replica) a Spanner instance is created with.
google_spanner_instance_partition: `google_spanner_instance_partition` reserves a dedicated slice of compute capacity within a Spanner instance for a specific database or set of databases, isolating its own performance from the rest of the instance.
google_spanner_session: `google_spanner_session` is a connection context Spanner client libraries create to execute reads, writes, and transactions against a database, pooled and reused across requests for efficiency.
google_sqladmin_backup_run: `google_sqladmin_backup_run` is a single completed or in-progress backup of a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_database: `google_sqladmin_database` is a single logical database within a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_instance: `google_sqladmin_instance` is a Cloud SQL instance -- a fully managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server database server.
google_sqladmin_ssl_cert: `google_sqladmin_ssl_cert` is a client SSL certificate issued for authenticating a connection to a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_user: `google_sqladmin_user` is a database user account on a Cloud SQL instance, used to authenticate connections to its own database(s).
google_storage_anywhere_cach: `google_storage_anywhere_cach` (Anywhere Cache) is a zonal, SSD-backed read cache for a Cloud Storage bucket, recently renamed Rapid Cache as part of the Cloud Storage Rapid family announced at Google Cloud Next '26 -- accelerating reads for AI training and analytics workloads without changing application code.
google_storage_bucket: `google_storage_bucket` is a Cloud Storage bucket, the top-level container that object(s) are uploaded into, with its own region, storage class, and access-control configuration.
google_storage_bucket_access_control: `google_storage_bucket_access_control` grants a specific access role (e.g. reader or owner) to an entity (a user, group, or `allUsers`) on an entire Cloud Storage bucket, via bucket-level ACLs.
google_storage_default_object_access_con: `google_storage_default_object_access_control` defines the ACL entry newly uploaded objects in a Cloud Storage bucket inherit by default, when the bucket uses fine-grained (rather than uniform) access control.
google_storage_folder: `google_storage_folder` is a real, hierarchical folder within a Cloud Storage bucket that has hierarchical namespace enabled, distinct from the flat, prefix-simulated "folders" of a standard bucket.
google_storage_hmac_key: `google_storage_hmac_key` is an HMAC credential pair for a Cloud Storage service account, used to authenticate requests through Cloud Storage's own S3-compatible XML API.
google_storage_managed_folder: `google_storage_managed_folder` defines a folder-like path prefix within a Cloud Storage bucket that its own IAM policy can be scoped to, letting different teams manage access to different prefixes within the same bucket.
google_storage_notification: `google_storage_notification` configures a Cloud Storage bucket to publish a Pub/Sub message whenever a specified object event (create, delete, and similar) occurs.
google_storage_object: `google_storage_object` is a single object (a file, blob, or piece of binary data) stored inside a Cloud Storage bucket.
google_storage_object_access_control: `google_storage_object_access_control` grants a specific access role (e.g. reader or owner) to an entity on a single Cloud Storage object, via object-level ACLs.
google_storage_rapid_cach: `google_storage_rapid_cach` (Rapid Cache, formerly Anywhere Cache) is a zonal, SSD-backed read cache for a Cloud Storage bucket, part of the Cloud Storage Rapid family announced at Google Cloud Next '26 -- accelerating reads for AI training, inference, and analytics workloads without requiring application code changes.
google_vmwareengine_cluster: `google_vmwareengine_cluster` is a cluster of node(s) within a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud, the unit VMware ESXi/vSAN compute and storage capacity is added to a private cloud in.
google_vmwareengine_datastore: `google_vmwareengine_datastore` is a vSAN datastore backing storage for VM(s) running on a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud's own cluster(s).
google_vmwareengine_external_access_rule: `google_vmwareengine_external_access_rule` is a firewall rule controlling traffic between the public internet and a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud's own external IP address(es).
google_vmwareengine_external_address: `google_vmwareengine_external_address` assigns a public IP address to a specific VM running inside a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud, via NAT from the private cloud's own external address range.
google_vmwareengine_hcx_activation_key: `google_vmwareengine_hcx_activation_key` generates a key used to activate a VMware HCX site connecting an on-premises VMware environment to a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud, for live workload migration.
google_vmwareengine_logging_server: `google_vmwareengine_logging_server` configures an external syslog server that a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud's own ESXi hosts forward log data to.
google_vmwareengine_management_dns_zone_: `google_vmwareengine_management_dns_zone_binding` binds a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud's own management DNS zone to a consumer VPC network, letting workloads there resolve vCenter/NSX management hostnames.
google_vmwareengine_network_peering: `google_vmwareengine_network_peering` peers a Google Cloud VMware Engine network with another VPC network, extending connectivity between the private cloud and Google Cloud-native resources or another VMware Engine network.
google_vmwareengine_network_policy: `google_vmwareengine_network_policy` configures internet access and external IP address behavior for a Google Cloud VMware Engine network.
google_vmwareengine_private_cloud: `google_vmwareengine_private_cloud` is the top-level Google Cloud VMware Engine resource -- a dedicated, VMware-based private cloud environment (vCenter, NSX-T, vSAN) running on Google Cloud infrastructure.
google_vmwareengine_private_connection: `google_vmwareengine_private_connection` establishes private connectivity between a Google Cloud VMware Engine network and an external network (e.g. an on-premises network reached via Cloud Interconnect or VPN).
google_vmwareengine_vmware_engine_networ: `google_vmwareengine_vmware_engine_network` is the Google Cloud VMware Engine-managed network that private cloud(s) attach to, providing the connectivity backbone between them and to peered VPC networks.
